## Consent by texting in, October 28, 2026

Casey, Oct 28, 2026, by voice: "I think if they text us, that's implied that they want to talk to us... if you say that okay to continue or something like that, somebody might not read that and then stop talking. So I think their reaching out is their consent, and then we just need to notify them if they want to stop receiving messages or maybe like after they send off their quote [request], a confirmation that they want us to reply with additional quotes, by text, email, or both. That goes to the link that has all the quote information." And on the pick page: "that doesn't need to be like blasted all over a page. That would just be in the terms that they would agree to." No simulation, persona pass or rehearsal was run. Research basis, AI research and not legal advice: the CTIA Messaging Principles and Best Practices treat a consumer who texts a business first as having opted in to a conversational reply about that request; the FCC treats a consumer's own text as prior express consent to informational, non-marketing replies about it (Ask Hava sends no marketing, TXT-008); the opt-in confirmation still carries the brand, the program, message frequency, rates, HELP and STOP, and the Terms and Privacy links.

- **D-419** Question: does a homeowner have to reply OK before Ask Hava keeps talking? Choice: no. The homeowner's first inbound text, or starting a web chat, is the opt-in for automated informational texts about their own request (CON-005); nothing waits for or asks for a reply of OK or YES. The first reply (still called the consent text, so BUILD_BRIEF's "consent text first on every path", `BUILD_BRIEF.md:445`, holds) carries the required disclosures in as few characters as possible and moves the conversation on: "Ask Hava: Got it. Next, a few quick questions. Ask Hava is not a contractor; you hire the business you pick directly. Automated texts about your request. Msg frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help. Terms: askhava.com/terms Privacy: askhava.com/privacy" (295 characters, GSM-7, 2 segments), and the first intake question follows at once as its own text; the Spanish version (303 characters, GSM-7, 2 segments) is built and tested but sent only while Spanish conversations are on (D-427). The emergency keyword check still runs first on every message (INT-002), so the safety or heat-safety text still goes before the first reply (CON-001). The fee line ("Free for you; the business you choose pays Ask Hava a set fee of $25 to $199, by quote size.") leaves the first text and stays in the SMS terms and on the help page; the fee is shown again beside every pick (PICK-016, WEB-026). The "18 or older" rule stays in the Terms, the web chat start and INT-038. A phone number typed in web chat is texted only after a Twilio Verify code proves the person holds it (CON-025), which replaces "until it replies OK" against SMS pumping and wrong numbers. Changed: CON-002, CON-003, CON-004, CON-005, CON-025, CON-026, CON-027, CON-031, INT-019, INT-025, INT-026, TXT-034, WORD-002, and INT-041, whose summary now says "It goes out in 2 hours. Reply EDIT to change it, or SEND to send it now." so no reply is needed there either; CON-006 withdrawn; `scripts/check_legal_docs.py` now requires "Msg frequency varies", the new first-reply line and "Texting Ask Hava, or starting a chat on askhava.com, is your OK to get automated texts about your own request." in place of "Reply OK to agree..." (its tests updated); the SMS terms, homeowner terms and privacy policy drafts updated. This is Casey's own decision, so it overrides the changes file's "Reply OK to agree to the Terms and start" (`sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:213`), which stays unedited because `sources/` is read-only; the requirements cite this decision instead. Supersedes the reply-OK parts of D-021, D-051, D-095, D-127, D-237, D-371 and D-398 (B16). Reason: Casey's decision above; a required OK loses people who never read it.
- **D-420** Question: with no reply-OK contract, when are the homeowner Terms accepted? Choice: on the private quote page, by picking (clickwrap): directly beside the Pick button, "By picking, you agree to the Terms" with an underlined link, and the acceptance is logged with its timestamp, the terms version and the request ID (TERMS-016); a pick by text ("<number> YES", PICK-015) is accepted the same way because every text that offers it ends "By picking, you agree to the Terms: askhava.com/terms" and the pick is logged with the channel "text". Changed: PICK-016, TERMS-001; the homeowner terms' electronic-signature section now names only the pick. Reason: Casey's decision above; the pick is the first moment anything binding happens.
- **D-421** Question: should the $100 liability cap be shown beside the Pick button? Choice: no. Beside the Pick button only "By picking, you agree to the Terms" (linked) appears; the "short version" line and the key-terms summary with the cap are removed from the pick page and from the homeowner terms' top; the cap stays, word for word, in homeowner terms section 10 under the bold heading "Limit of liability", so it is easy to find from the link. Changed: PICK-016, TERMS-004 (the cap's place), the homeowner terms draft and `scripts/check_legal_docs.py` (the PICK-016 key-terms phrase is no longer required in the homeowner terms). Reason: Casey Oct 28, 2026: "that doesn't need to be like blasted all over a page. That would just be in the terms that they would agree to."
- **D-422** Question: how does the homeowner choose how quote updates arrive? Choice: TXT-018 replaces "Want updates by email too?": after the INT-041 summary step, once the job cards go out and the TXT-032 text is sent, one question is asked once: "Ask Hava: How should we send quote updates? 1) Text 2) Email 3) Both. Every update links to your private quote page."; no answer, or an unclear one, keeps text (the default) and the question is never asked again; 2 or 3 asks one follow-up, "What email should we use? We never share it with businesses.", checked for format and confirmed by the first email's delivery, a hard bounce switching updates back to text with a note on the quote page; email updates follow the existing email rules (SEC-028 footer, an unsubscribe link in each update email, one suppression list across text, email and portal, CON-035); safety texts, codes and direct replies to the homeowner's own texts still go by text. Reason: Casey's decision above ("by text, email, or both. That goes to the link that has all the quote information").
- **D-423** Question: is a separate opt-out notice needed? Choice: no; the first reply already says "Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help", and the STOP and revocation rules stay as they are: FCC 26-67 (effective November 25, 2026) handling (CON-032), one stop list across text, email and portal (CON-035) and the bare STOP confirmation (CON-009). No spec change beyond D-419. Reason: Casey's "we just need to notify them if they want to stop receiving messages".
- **D-424** Question: what does the Twilio question say now? Choice: the short version in `docs/for-casey-review.md` and `/home/claude/hhq/outputs/send_drafts/Twilio_question.md`: subject "Eligibility check before A2P 10DLC registration – customer care texts"; the homeowner texts first, the first reply carries the disclosures, only that homeowner's own request is texted, no marketing, businesses get job requests by email only and are never texted; two questions: eligibility as Customer Care (or conversational) with the inbound text as the opt-in, and whether the privacy sentence "Your first name and address go only to the one business you choose" triggers errors 30871 or 30951; signed "Ask Hava (LLC being formed)" with no personal name (WORD-021). The business-texting questions are gone. PREBUILD item 6 sends this version. No spec change. Reason: businesses are email-only; a shorter question gets a clearer answer.
- **D-425** Question (PREBUILD B11): trademark. Choice: skip for now; revisit if Ask Hava grows beyond Lake Havasu City or another "Ask Hava" appears. No spec change; the WORD-023 rule still governs any later application's wording. Reason: Casey Oct 28, 2026: "We can skip trademark for now."
- **D-426** Question (PREBUILD B13): insurance. Choice: later, after the business is fully working; it is no longer listed as a step before the first paid introduction. No spec change. Reason: Casey Oct 28, 2026: "We'll [skip] insurance for now. We'll work all that out after we have a fully working business."
- **D-427** Question (PREBUILD B17): Spanish. Casey doesn't speak Spanish and knows no one who does: "your recommendation is going to have to be best". Choice: launch English-only for conversations. New TXT-039: an owner-portal setting "Spanish conversations", off at launch; while it is off every homeowner text, web-chat message and email comes from the English template even when the message reads as Spanish, and business notices are English (BIZ-018's Spanish choice hidden), except that the Spanish safety texts stay on: the safety, heat-safety and other emergency texts (INT-004, INT-031, INT-034, INT-037, INT-042 prompts), plus the AYUDA reply and the Spanish opt-out confirmation, which carriers expect for Spanish keywords; Spanish opt-out words are always honored (CON-008). Before launch each Spanish text that stays on is checked by back-translation through two separate AIs (ChatGPT and Grok), each translating the Spanish back into English on its own; the check passes only when both back-translations match the English template's meaning, and the date and result are logged in `docs/decisions.md`; a text that fails is fixed and checked again. The Spanish conversation templates are still built and tested (TXT-001, TXT-003). - **D-428** Question: which tasks build this, and what stays open? Choice: test-design rows TD-CON-01, TD-CON-02, TD-CON-10, TD-CON-11, TD-CON-14, TD-CON-15, TD-CON-18, TD-CON-23, TD-INT-08, TD-INT-10, TD-INT-23, TD-TXT-01, TD-TXT-06, TD-PICK-30, TD-WORD-05, TD-TERMS-01 and journey J1 changed, and TD-CON-24 (no reply-OK anywhere; emergency check first), TD-TXT-23 (the updates question) and TD-TXT-24 (Spanish conversations setting) added; T038 builds consent by the first text, T026 the Spanish conversations setting (TXT-039), T156 the updates question (TXT-018, moved from T047), T055 the pick-page terms line (PICK-016), T103 the web-chat opt-in and code check (CON-025), T161 the 2-segment and no-reply-OK scans (CON-031, CON-004), and T111 and T112 the drafts; prompts regenerated. ## Fix round 14: packaged jobs, October 28, 2026

Casey, Oct 28, 2026, after the walkthrough review (relayed in `docs/handoff/HANDOFF.md` section 5): the job going to the business and the quotes going back should be "as well packaged as possible", so homeowners feel the service knows exactly what they need and businesses get a pre-packaged job they'd otherwise pay a well-versed receptionist to gather. On own-or-rent: "If you call a plumber, they don't ask you if you own the home." On heat: "they are well aware the AC went out and it's hot." His four answers on the rework plan (`docs/handoff/rework-plan.md`), Oct 28, 2026: photos "Photos now, AI later"; address "She OKs it at the pick"; tax ruling "Ruling on the later list"; 911 list "Fire-truck list only". Then: "Do everything that you recommend for all the following questions." New inputs: the Grok trade knowledge base (`docs/catalog/trade_kb/`, AI research, not legal advice) and the ChatGPT sales-tax report (AI research, not tax advice; summarized in `docs/for-casey-review.md`). No simulation, persona pass or rehearsal was run. These choices reverse earlier rules on purpose; each reversal is named below.

- **D-429** Question: what is the goal of this round? Choice: every requirement is re-read through Casey's "as well packaged as possible" lens; the plan is `docs/handoff/rework-plan.md` (homeowner H1 to H14, business B1 to B7, owner O1 to O4, AI A1 to A5, gaps G1 to G23), applied in this one round; decisions D-430 to D-449 record each change. Reason: Casey's direction above.
- **D-430** Question: may the AI write words people read? Reverses AI-006, TXT-004 and CARD-007's "never free text" (D-373 for cards; D-080 and D-412 kept for what the AI may see). Choice: yes, inside fixed limits (new AI-019): while "AI on scrubbed text" is on (AI-008), the AI may (a) reword the next question from the question bank to fit what the homeowner already said, or ask one follow-up the bank's expert brief allows, (b) write the job card and the project file from her scrubbed words, answers and photo notes, and (c) write the concept-image prompt (D-433); it never diagnoses, names a cause, prices, estimates cost, judges safety or urgency, recommends a business, promises anything, or says anything about a business or a quote; every AI-written card is shown to the homeowner and approved (or auto-sent after the INT-041 wait) before it goes; code checks every AI output for contact details (CARD-008), prices and dollar amounts, cause words ("probably", "likely", "sounds like", "needs a new") and the WORD-022 list, and a failure falls back to the fixed template; every text keeps the fixed first reply, opt-out, HELP, code, pick and money templates; AI quote summaries stay off (PICK-003, D-373 unchanged). Reason: Casey's "well-versed receptionist"; legal Memo 4's points (no diagnosing or pricing in Ask Hava's own words; the homeowner approves the card) handled by the limits and the approval step.
- **D-431** Question: where do the expert questions come from? Choice: the Grok knowledge base is kept in `docs/catalog/trade_kb/` (37 trade files, foundation files, 370 test messages) as the expert brief for intake; each question set in `docs/catalog/question_bank.yaml` names its knowledge-base trade (`kb_trade`), its photo asks and its quote format; a set may hold 3 to 8 questions (was 6) in price-impact order; the fixed bank stays the fallback whenever AI is off; the 370 test messages join the golden set (OPS-040); the knowledge base's safety steps are not used where they give health or safety advice (D-436); the `intake_questions` fallback lists in `categories.yaml` are removed (G20). Changed: INT-039, LIC-040, OPS-040, `scripts/check_catalog.py`. Reason: Casey's "thinks like a licensed pro in every trade".
- **D-432** Question (rework question 1, G2): how do photos work before a zero-retention agreement? Reverses CARD-013. Choice: photos from day one, never required: intake asks for the job type's 2 or 3 photos (question bank `photos`) by picture text or by an upload link on the homeowner's portal page, says "No photo is fine too", and never asks for one during a 911-list situation (INT-004); every photo is stripped of metadata (PRIV-014) and checked on Ask Hava's own server (no outside AI) for faces, people, house numbers, plates and readable text, and a flagged photo is blurred or left off with a note; the homeowner sees each photo as it will appear and can remove it before the card goes; picture texts are copied off the texting provider and deleted there once stored; photos go on the job card and the job page; the AI reads photos (quality, what they show) only after the zero-retention agreement is signed and the AI-018 photo sentence is live, and until then a photo is never judged for quality, one re-ask being sent only when the file is unreadable or too small. Changed: new INT-044, CARD-013, CARD-014, AI-016, PRIV-013, PRIV-015, PICK-022. Reason: Casey Oct 28, 2026: "Photos now, AI later".
- **D-433** Question: inspiration images, project file and concept images? Choice: new INT-045: in a category whose quote format is a range and that is marked `design: true` (painting, pavers and hardscape, epoxy floors, and any later remodel category), intake asks "Have any pictures of the look you want? Screenshots are fine."; inspiration images are handled as photos (D-432) and, once AI may read photos, read into a short project file (size, layout, style, finishes, for example "standard 5 by 8 bath, this layout, minimalist modern, these textures"), and before that she describes the look in a few words; new INT-046: in those categories, while the owner switch "Concept images" is on, Ask Hava may make one concept image from the written project file only (never her photos), labeled on the image and beside it "AI-generated, not exact, may not be feasible", asks "Is this the kind of thing you want?", allows up to 3 rounds of changes, and puts the image on the card with the same label; the image provider is chosen at the account checkpoint (its terms recorded like AI-008's) and the switch is off until then. Reason: her approval covers what businesses see.

We've noted your request so we can add businesses." (INT-017, TXT-032); each no-coverage request emails the owner inbox (new OPS-041) with trade, town and the count so far that month, and the weekly digest rolls them up; recruiting stays email or in person (BIZ-048). Reason: Casey's direction item 9.
- **D-436** Question (rework question 4, G13): which situations get a 911 text? Reverses INT-031 (heat-safety text), the 211 entry, INT-034's water and power-line lines, INT-035, INT-037's chirp text and INT-042's trade safety prompts. Choice: only the fire-truck list: a gas or propane smell or hiss, a CO alarm going off, smoke, fire or flames, a sparking, smoking or burning outlet, cord, switch or panel, and a downed or sparking power line; one fixed text, "Ask Hava: Ask Hava isn't an emergency service. If you smell gas, see smoke or fire, a CO alarm is going off, or a power line is down, get everyone out and call 911 from outside. Reply SAFE when you're safe.", from English and Spanish templates; the SAFE hold stays (INT-005); no symptom, health, heat, water, shutoff, utility-number or appliance advice anywhere; floods, burst pipes, AC out and no heat go straight to the businesses in that trade that take urgent jobs, through the normal urgent choice (INT-006); a numbered "smell" answer asks "What kind of smell? 1) Gas or rotten egg 2) Burning 3) Something else", 1 or 2 sending the 911 text; the safety-contacts file (INT-036) is withdrawn because no text names a number; the site's statement says plainly that Ask Hava is not an emergency service and doesn't judge what needs an emergency response (WEB-022). - **D-437** Question: keep own-or-rent? Choice: no. Withdrawn: INT-028, TXT-028, CARD-011; the rental flag leaves INT-018, INT-029 and AI-010. Research (AI research, not legal advice): no Arizona or federal rule requires a quote-request service to ask; landlord permission and lien exposure fall on the business that does the work (an Arizona appeals court let a contractor hired by a tenant recover against the owner's property, *Wang Electric, Inc. v. Smoke Tree Resort, LLC*, 2012); the EPA lead-renovation rule puts the pamphlet duty on the renovator. Reason: Casey: "If you call a plumber, they don't ask you if you own the home."
- **D-438** Question: how long are texts, and what is on the portal? Reverses PICK-041's "no reviews" and the long first-quote text. Choice: new TXT-040: every homeowner update text is one or two short sentences plus her portal link (her private quote page, PICK-010); the portal holds every quote, each business's name, license numbers and record link, its Google and Yelp review links (as links only: Ask Hava shows no stars, counts or ranking), the card, and the not-a-contractor statement; TXT-016 shrinks to "Ask Hava: Your first quote is in for request <n>. More may come. See it here: <link>" plus the LIST line; G1: the portal top and the first-quote text say "Free for you. The business you pick pays Ask Hava a set introduction fee." (CON-003), PICK-016's terms line beside the button stays alone. Reason: Casey's direction items 6 and 7.
- **D-439** Question: what does sign-up collect? Choice: new BIZ-052: the Google Business Profile link and the Yelp page link (each optional, checked to be on the matching domain and to open), and every license number the business holds (ROC, Department of Agriculture, Board of Technical Registration), shown on every quote card and the portal; changing one is checked the same way; free-text directions to other channels stay banned (BIZ-022). Reason: Casey's direction item 7.
- **D-440** Question: does Ask Hava schedule anything? Choice: no. Withdrawn: PICK-025 (who lets the business in, on-site contact, lockbox); the call-window choice leaves PICK-018, PICK-031 and TXT-030 (no TIMES); the window is fixed at 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Arizona time ("Now" on a job chosen as an emergency), which the PICK-021 refund line's "inside their window" means; homeowner texts drop "has until <time> to confirm" detail (PICK-045 becomes "Ask Hava: Done. <Business> has your pick. We'll text you when they accept."); after acceptance the business reaches her and they set the time. Reason: Casey's direction item 8.
- **D-441** Question (G4, G17): how do quotes compare? Reverses PICK-002's free choice of quote type. Choice: new PICK-053: each category names one quote format in `categories.yaml` (`quote_format`): `range` (replacements, remodels, installs), `monthly` (ongoing services), `tiers` (up to 3 named packages, for example detailing or cleaning), `firm` (small fixed jobs) or `diagnostic_visit` (repairs that need a look: a visit fee plus an estimate on site), and a job type may name its own (`job_type_formats`, for example faucet replacement `firm` inside plumbing repair); every quote for a job type uses the same format, so they line up; a site-visit fee is a quote type only in `diagnostic_visit` categories (FEE-004), so a site visit can't stand in for a range on a big job; a business that can't price without seeing it still gives a range and ticks "Range to be confirmed on site"; a tiers quote's fee is set by the tier she picks; PICK-038's mixed-type sentence becomes "the picked quote was a different type of quote from yours." Choice: three layers. (3) A cold read (WORD-028): every task prompt and `BUILD_BRIEF.md` section 7 step 4 add a reviewer that sees only the finished copy, reads it aloud and flags anything machine-written; the standard is a local person explaining it to a neighbour (`docs/voice.md`). - **D-453** Question (Casey Oct 28, 2026, after sending "Ask Hava — Technology Stack and Programming Language Directive" and asking whether Rust has benefits beyond build complexity: "We will use rust and deal with the more complex build"; then, asked how much and how pages are built, "All of the server" and "Rust builds the pages"): what does the build use? Choice: Rust for all server code, replacing Python 3.12 and FastAPI (BUILD_BRIEF.md §4, :101 to :122, rewritten line for line so every citation still points at the same line). Axum and Tokio; Askama templates checked at compile time and autoescaped, so pages still work without JavaScript (WEB-001); SQLx with queries checked against the schema; SQL migration files `migrations/0NNN_<slug>.sql`; reqwest clients behind one trait per vendor; serde with `deny_unknown_fields`; small TypeScript compiled by `tsc --strict` for browser extras; Playwright for TypeScript with axe-core for e2e and accessibility; proptest, trybuild and cargo-mutants; clippy, rustfmt, cargo-audit, cargo-deny and npm audit. One Cargo workspace with one crate per module, so the layer rules (architecture §4) are compile errors; `automod` declares each crate's files, so tasks add files without editing a shared `lib.rs`; `Cargo.lock` and `app/server/src/main.rs` become the shared files (replacing `app/main.py`). The benefits Casey chose it for are written as requirements: SEC-029 (workspace, `unsafe_code` forbidden, clippy denied), SEC-030 (contact release only with a `ReleaseProof` that only `payments` can create; compile-fail test), SEC-031 (statuses are exhaustive enums), plus SEC-032 (stand-ins served over HTTP by new harness task T167, so one client runs against stand-in, sandbox and live) and SEC-033 (the directive's server-authority and no-secrets-in-the-browser tests); SEC-021 now names the Rust and npm audits. What stays Python: the build tooling in `scripts/`, the runner, the stand-ins, the twin and its gate (which reaches the Rust rules through a `rules_bridge` binary, T074), the document tests and the stand-in contract tests; none of it runs in production. Verified in this session on a scratch workspace with the pinned versions in architecture §11 on Rust 1.99.0: it builds, clippy passes with warnings denied, Askama escaped a planted `<script>`, a trybuild test showed a paid-pick type cannot be built outside its crate, SQLx applied a lower-numbered migration added after a higher one, cargo-audit found no vulnerabilities (one unmaintained build-time crate, ignored with its reason) and cargo-deny passed (architecture §11). Not adopted from the directive: React and Next.js (Casey chose server-built pages), OpenAPI and generated TypeScript types (no separate front end to keep in sync). Every task's owned paths were remapped (`app/<m>/<f>.py` to `app/<m>/src/<f>.rs`, tests to their layer crates, e2e and a11y to `.spec.ts`), and the protected `scripts/validate_tasks.py`, its test, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the task template were changed in this owner-approved plan change. An independent Opus review of the whole change found that one owner per crate manifest could not work (a crate lists a path dependency only once that crate exists), that four test-layer crates would have no targets, that `.sqlx/` and CI Postgres had no owner, that trybuild needs owned `.stderr` files, that test crates could not reach crate internals, that SEC-033 sat too early, and that two clippy lints were misnamed or too broad; all were fixed: crate manifests, the workspace `Cargo.toml`, `.sqlx/`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` became shared paths; new T168 (test-layer crates, ahead of every task that followed T009) and harness T169 (CI Postgres pinning, coverage, Playwright in Ally, eslint, the TypeScript build in the image); a per-crate `testing` feature exposes internals to the test crates only; the Postgres service and SQLX_OFFLINE are in `ci.yml` now; SEC-033 moved to T120; `clippy.toml` sets the 50-line limit; the wildcard lint is scoped to status modules plus a source scan. D-451's note that `BUILD_BRIEF.md:106` stays unedited is superseded: that line now names Askama. Reason: Casey chose Rust for the compiler-enforced guarantees on money, contact release and job statuses, and accepted the more complex build.

## Encryption of customer details, October 28, 2026

Casey, Oct 28, 2026: "One thing I would like is for all the customer info to be encrypted sent to the buisness and all data we keep will be encrypted." He had ChatGPT propose options, Claude checked them against this plan, and Casey then said "Do what you think is best".

- **D-454** Question: what changes so customer details are encrypted on the way to the business and wherever they are kept? Already in the plan and unchanged: the field-encrypted contact vault with associated data and key versions (PRIV-002, architecture section 8), the blind phone index, audited plaintext reads, encrypted backups (PRIV-018), per-person business sign-in with a new-device code (SEC-004), server-side authority on every request (SEC-033), and the Safeguards-style security program and incident plan in `docs/legal/`. Choice: (1) the release email no longer carries any homeowner detail: it says the job is confirmed and links to sign-in, and the first name, job address and any shared email are shown only in the signed-in business portal (PICK-024 rewritten; the text for businesses that chose text drops "in your email"), because ordinary email is not end-to-end encrypted and sits in forwarded or shared inboxes (threat-model I15, R15); (2) photos are encrypted by the app under the vault key before they reach object storage and are served only through the app's own photo route behind a short-lived signed link, never a direct storage link (new PRIV-023; PRIV-014 amended); (3) every page that shows a homeowner's details or job photos sends `Cache-Control: no-store` and loads no third-party script, and no URL, email subject, push notice or text carries a homeowner detail (new SEC-034); (4) the privacy policy says plainly that texts and ordinary email are not end-to-end encrypted and points people to askhava.com for sensitive details; (5) SEC-001's "plain environment variables" is read as `BUILD_BRIEF.md:62` to `BUILD_BRIEF.md:65` allows: keys live in the app host's secret variables, never in code, logs or files. Not adopted now: an outside key service (AWS KMS or Google Cloud KMS with envelope encryption). It keeps the master key off the app host, but on Railway the cloud login would itself sit in a host variable; the clean form needs Render Pro's AWS workload sign-in (about $25 a month more). It is recorded as an option to decide with the Railway-or-Render choice at the account checkpoint (D-094), behind the existing key-version field so it can be added without re-encrypting by hand. Also not adopted: per-job data keys as a way to erase purged jobs from backups, because each backup also holds that job's wrapped key, so a restore would bring the data back; purged details leave backups only when the backup window expires, which the privacy policy already allows. Two checks added to the account checkpoint: the chosen host encrypts the database, volumes and backups at rest, and the Claude Console workspace has zero data retention in force before AI-008 is switched on. Reason: Casey asked for encryption in transit to the business and at rest everywhere; email was the one place homeowner details left an encrypted, access-controlled system, and the photo and caching changes close the remaining gaps at no running cost.

## Fix round 16: ChatGPT's stress test of the hand-run test, October 28, 2026

Casey sent the plan, the playbook and fix round 15 to ChatGPT for an outside attack ("Ask Hava Pre-Build Stress Test: Deep Research Review", Oct 28, 2026) and brought the answer back; his standing instruction is "So do what you recommend and identify what needs to be done before the build starts".

- **D-468** Question: ChatGPT found that the hand-run test (D-455) could not answer its own money question, because a stated "it would be worth it" isn't payment (stated willingness to pay runs well above real buying); that jobs from people Casey knows would inflate demand; that one quote proves routing, not choice; that a 4-hour median hides slow tails; that Casey's own nudges could make the test look better than the system; that about 25 to 40 requests give wide error bars; that a November start tests winter Havasu only; and that 8 hours a week is already near the monthly time limit. Choice: `docs/pilot/hand-run-test.md` is rewritten: four questions (demand, choice, payment, time); a rules tab fixed before the test (request, source class Seeded, Partner or Organic, routable, pushed trade, valid quote, active business, nudge, season); weeks 1 to 3 helped and free, weeks 4 to 6 hands off and paid, with picked businesses in the pushed trades paying the real fee by payment link before the details, and no free first win in the test; a scorecard on Organic requests, 2-or-more-quote share, median and 75th-percentile first quote, picks among requests with 2 or more quotes, active (quoting) businesses, self-serve activation, real payments by 5 or more businesses, hands-off versus helped quote rates, and minutes per request; results reported as a winter test; homeowner details deleted 90 days after it ends. Company setup (the LLC, EIN and a live Stripe account) moves to the start of the test, so the paid weeks can run; this supersedes D-467 item (4). In the build: OPS-039 adds the 2-and-3-quote shares, the 75th-percentile first-quote time, picks among requests with 2 or more quotes, active businesses per trade, and quotes per win; OPS-027's crowding flag also shows quotes per win; WEB-028 waits for 50 requests and shows its date range and trade count. All service categories stay open (D-459, Casey's call); the pushed trades are the ones judged. Not adopted: dropping the free first win at launch (D-465 keeps it and judges the pilot on businesses paying again within 60 days; the test itself has no free win), and moving the Twilio question later (an answer takes days and costs nothing to ask). The phone-recruiting rule is restated as a legal uncertainty under A.R.S. 44-1271 and 44-1272, still with no calls. Reason: payment, organic demand and choice are what the build depends on, and the test now measures each with something a person did rather than said.
- **D-469** Question (Casey Oct 28, 2026: "Want to have all set before we go live. We can fill them all with a test environment of fake buisnessed and responses to make sure it all works"): how is the hand-run test rehearsed before any real person is involved? - **D-470** Question (ChatGPT's "Ask Hava Legal Research Report", Oct 28, 2026, which Casey asked for and brought back): what has to change before the paid test weeks and before launch? Its findings: no Arizona statute, ROC rule or decision bars a neutral fixed introduction fee, so it is likely lawful but not settled (A.R.S. 32-1101, 32-1154); Ask Hava stays outside contractor status only while it never bids, prices, negotiates scope, schedules, supervises, guarantees or takes payment for work; TPT on the fee is likely not owed but unresolved, and a city business license is a separate requirement; a sign-up note plus a payment click can form a contract but is fragile; the future-state privacy policy and SMS terms describe tools the hand-run test doesn't use; job-card emails should meet CAN-SPAM anyway; and the FTC Safeguards Rule likely treats Ask Hava as a finder, while whether one-off homeowners are "customers" is unclear, and the under-5,000 exception removes only four specific requirements. Choice: before the paid weeks, (1) new `docs/pilot/paid-pilot-terms.md`, one page, accepted by every business on a form with an unticked box, version and time, before any paid-week card; the payment link and a receipt repeat the version; (2) new `docs/pilot/pilot-privacy-notice.md`, describing only Google Forms, Sheets, Gmail and Stripe, linked from the request form; (3) a CAN-SPAM footer with the postal address and an unsubscribe on every job card; (4) the Lake Havasu City business license (and home-occupation form if run from home) before week 4 at the latest; (5) refund wording that doesn't assume a phone call, since the test shares email only; (6) a licensed-only rule for permit-heavy work and no splitting of a project to fit the handyman limit. Before launch: CON-005 and the SMS terms make web-chat text consent explicit (typing a mobile number and its code), the privacy policy's breach line follows the law, the business terms' tax line says tax owed is included rather than implying none is owed, and the security program gains an applicability review, vendor-contract safeguards, a data inventory and a label on voluntary controls. Not changed: the tiered fee (a single flat fee would be cleaner, which goes to the re-plan pass with the fee level), and the tax path, which stays the 8.6% set-aside while Casey chooses between an ADOR private ruling (the report's advice) and his own research (his earlier call). Reason: the report found no legal blocker to the paid test on these facts, and each change makes a promise provable or a document true for the day it's used.
