- **D-588** Question (T009, October 30, 2026): what do the binaries and `deny.toml` do before any module exists? Choice: `server` installs the TLS provider, reads `PORT` (a host variable, not an `ASKHAVA_*` setting) and exits 1 with "PORT is not set" or "PORT is not a port number" without echoing the value, binds `0.0.0.0:$PORT` and serves an empty router with graceful shutdown on SIGINT or SIGTERM; `/healthz` is left to T106, which owns it. `worker` installs the provider and idles until SIGINT or SIGTERM, then exits 0, until T013 adds the claim loop, so a host does not restart-loop it. Both register their signal handlers before serving, so a signal-handler failure stops the start. `deny.toml`: section 11's license list, `private.ignore` for the unpublished first-party crates, crates.io as the only source, wildcards denied except workspace paths, duplicate versions a warning, `askama_axum` and `serde_yaml` banned with reasons, and RUSTSEC-2026-0374 (`basic-toml`, compile time only through `askama_derive`) ignored with a reason and a review date of 2027-04-30; until askama enters the lockfile, cargo-deny warns that this advisory was not encountered, which does not fail the check. Run on the branch: `GET /` answered 404, SIGTERM to `server` and SIGINT to `worker` each exited 0, and a missing or bad `PORT` exited 1. Reason: `docs/architecture.md` section 2 (main.rs, worker.rs) and section 11 (`deny.toml`), within T009's files.
- **D-590** Question (T219, harness, October 30, 2026; the skeleton trial's finding D8, `docs/audit/rust-skeleton-trial-2026-10-29.md`): which shapes must `scripts/check_rust_rules.py` catch before the first `status.rs` lands? Choice: it reads each Rust file as code, comments and strings (`/* */` and nested comments, raw strings, char literals), so `unsafe {` in a comment or string no longer fails and `/* TODO */` does; it fails on an alias import (`Status as S`), a variant import, `let Status::X = s else`, a rustfmt-split `matches!`, `Status::X == s`, `assert_eq!`/`assert_ne!` naming a variant, a binding catch-all (`other =>`) in a status module or in a match that also has a status arm, `escape = "none"` or `ext = "txt"` in a `#[template]` attribute, and `{% filter safe %}`; template files of any extension under `app/*/templates/` are scanned. A status module is a file named `status.rs`; status enums are every enum a `status.rs` defines (any name) and `*Status` enums elsewhere except under `app/adapters/`, so a vendor's `*Status` enum no longer marks its file as a status module. Paths containing `/ui/` are scanned like any other (only `target/` is skipped); the old trybuild skip test was replaced by `test_ui_paths_are_scanned`, a spec change this decision logs. Locked file `scripts/check_rust_rules.py` rewritten with `kit/plan.lock`. Reason: SEC-031, TD-SEC-12; each shape has a planted-case test in `tests/test_check_rust_rules.py`.

- **D-591** Question (T219 review follow-up): which further shapes must `scripts/check_rust_rules.py` catch? Choice: `true =>` and `false =>` are not catch-all arms, and `| _ =>` / `| other =>` are; a status arm may be wrapped (`Some(JobStatus::Open) =>`, tuple arms, `x @ JobStatus::Open =>`); `== &JobStatus::Open`, `!= Some(JobStatus::Open)` and the reversed forms are comparisons; a `#[template]` with a non-HTML `path` extension, `|safe` or `|e("none")` in an inline `source`, and `|e("none")` / `|escape("none")` in a template file fail. Reason: SEC-031, SEC-011, TD-SEC-12 (SEC-031, D-590); planted-case tests in `tests/test_check_rust_rules.py`. Locked file rewritten with `kit/plan.lock`.

- **D-595** Question (T175, October 30, 2026): FEE-032 and TD-FEE-16 say only `payments` imports the payments adapter, but the adapter lives in `adapters` and `server` is the composition root that builds every adapter from settings; how does the architecture test recognise the payments adapter, and who else may name it? Choice: a source file names the payments adapter when a path that starts at `askhava_adapters` (a `use` tree or a qualified name) has a segment `payments` or a segment containing `stripe` (any case), or holds an alias (`as`, including `use askhava_adapters as ad;`) or a glob (`*`), which could hide it; `adapters` (its home), `payments` and `server` (which wires it) may, every other crate and every test-layer crate may not, so other crates name each adapter item by its full path. Reason: FEE-032, TD-FEE-16; `adapters` keeps the payments adapter at `api::payments` (section 7's adapter name) so the scan finds it. - **D-596** Question (T175, October 30, 2026; TD-SEC-03's architecture case, D-491): how does a source scan tell an adapter method that acts outside from one that only reads, so it can demand an idempotency key (SEC-018)? Choice: every `fn` declared in a `trait` in the `adapters` crate must take a parameter whose name or type contains `idempotency` (any case), unless its name starts with `fetch_`, `get_`, `list_`, `read_`, `check_` or `lookup_`, the read-only prefixes (not `verify_`: the verify adapter sends codes by text and email, so its methods take the key); an adapter method that sends, creates, charges, refunds, calls, writes or deletes is named otherwise and takes the key. Reason: SEC-018 and section 4 rule 6; a naming rule is checkable without `syn` (not on the allow-list), and the default is strict, so a new acting method without a key fails. An AI call that only reads (T024) is named `read_`. Planted cases `no_idempotency` and `verify_send_code`.

- **D-597** Question (T175, October 30, 2026): what may a test-layer crate or `askhava-fixtures` depend on, which files may name the mints, and what does T175 leave to T226? Choice: `server` and the test-layer crates (`askhava-integration`, `askhava-security`, `askhava-recovery-tests`, `askhava-fixtures`) may depend on any module crate in `kit/layers.json` but never on `askhava-server` or another test crate, except `askhava-fixtures`, which any crate may take as a dev-dependency and any test-layer crate as a dependency (T010's fake data); `core` may depend on no first-party crate. `ReleaseMint`, `release_mint`, `SessionMint` and `session_mint` may be named in `tests/security/ui/` (the compile-fail cases must name them) and nowhere else outside their crates. No member but `core` may have an `optional = true` dependency, as each is an implicit feature. The whole-word `unsafe` token fails in every member's Rust source, comments and strings excluded, besides the forbid lint. The cross-schema key and the non-literal `sqlx::query` named in T175's goal are checked by `architecture_migrations.rs` (T226), as the same goal assigns; T175's file has none of that code. Known limits: the integration tests (FEE-032's flow tests) are a test-layer crate and so may not name the payments adapter, which they reach only through `payments`; and the `deny_unknown_fields` structs are collected per crate, so a route input of a strict struct from another crate fails, and `Path<T>` inputs are not checked. The file is about 820 lines after rustfmt against a 600-line budget, close to the second trial's estimate for the checks it holds (`docs/audit/rust-trial-2-2026-10-29.md` finding 15); the case tables are `#[rustfmt::skip]` rows so each planted case is one line.
- **D-600** Question (T226, October 30, 2026): how exactly do the migration checks and the SQL scan of `architecture_migrations.rs` read the files? Choice: a migration is named `0NNN_<slug>.sql` (four digits, a lower-case slug; `.up.sql`/`.down.sql` fail, as migrations are forward-only) and no number is used twice; its header is `-- <module> (T###)` on line 1, or line 2 after `-- no-transaction`, `<module>` a schema in `kit/layers.json`, and any text may follow the `)`; the order check compares every pair, not only pairs that touch one schema as section 2 said before, since T226's goal states it so and the 70 migrations planned in `kit/tasks.json` already pass it (checked by script on this date); section 2 now says so. SQL is lexed with `--` and nested `/* */` comments and `'…'`/`E'…'` strings removed, unquoted names folded to lower case and quoted names as written; dollar-quoted bodies are lexed as SQL, not removed, so a function body cannot hide another schema; each body is lexed on its own up to its matching closing `$tag$`, so an odd apostrophe inside cannot swallow the SQL after it. Another module's schema fails as `x.`, after `SCHEMA` (lists included) and after `search_path` (a quoted value is split on commas); `public` fails outside `core`; `REFERENCES x.` has its own message. The same reference rule runs on the SQL of `query!`, `query_as!`, `query_scalar!` and the file of `query_file*!` in every `app/` crate, the crate's folder being its schema (Arch 4 rule 3), with `(`, `[` or `{` after the `!`. The SQL-form scan fails on `AssertSqlSafe`, `QueryBuilder`, `raw_sql`, `copy_in_raw`, `copy_out_raw` and any `query*_unchecked` anywhere in `app/`, and, in a path or `use` tree after `sqlx::`, on a function form (`query`, `query_as`, `query_scalar` and their `_with` forms) not followed by `!`, any name containing `Executor`, a glob, `sqlx as` and `sqlx::{self as …}`; so `use sqlx::query;` fails even though it also imports the macro. The migration checks pass on an empty or missing `migrations/` folder, and asserting the folder whenever `kit/tasks.json` plans a migration would fail before the first migration task runs; so a missing root `migrations/` folder fails only once an `app/` file uses `migrate!` (the migrator that embeds them), the simplest check that is sound at every point of the build. Known limits: `set_config('search_path', …)` is not seen; dynamic SQL held in a string inside a `DO` block or function body (`EXECUTE 'SELECT … FROM picks.x'`) is not read, as strings are removed; `U&"…"` Unicode-escaped names are not decoded, so `U&"\0070icks".x` is not seen; a table-qualified column whose table shares a module's name (`quotes.id`) fails and must use an alias; the lexer helpers repeat those of `architecture.rs`, as T226 owns one file. Reason: SEC-029, TD-SEC-10, D-491, D-492. The file is about 660 lines after rustfmt against a 500-line budget (about 710 after the review fixes), the 38 planted cases being one `#[rustfmt::skip]` row each, plus one test for the missing folder.

- **D-620** Question (harness plan change, October 30, 2026; stages C and D of two lanes, after D-515's lane-ready state and leases and D-530's per-task decision numbers): how does the runner work two tasks at once safely, roughly doubling throughput, with the switch left as a pure configuration flip? Gaps found: with strict up-to-date branches (ruleset protect-main) one task's merge leaves the other task's pull request behind or conflicted, and only a person merged `main` in; the cycle claimed only lane "1", refused every claim while any task was MERGE_PENDING, and returned `lease_live` before resolving any merge; one backup-runner job ran at a time (concurrency group `backup-runner`); pacing counted only finished attempts; `--after` and the hand-off read lane "1" only, and the worker heartbeat called `renewal_due` for lane "1", so a lane-2 lease would never have been renewed. Kind: conflict. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` read "- the runner does **one task per session, one session at a time**. There's no parallel building, so there are no state races or merge conflicts;", `BUILD_BRIEF.md:210` read "- parallelism exists only inside a session, as read-only review subagents.", `BUILD_BRIEF.md:222` read "- a rejected (non-fast-forward) push means another runner won, so this one exits. Git's own rule is the lock;" and `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224` read "- **nothing new is claimed while any task is `MERGE_PENDING`.** One task is in flight at a time, so a branch can never fall behind another task's merge. If `main` moved anyway (for example, Casey edited a file), the runner merges `main` into the task branch with a normal merge commit; it never rebases and force-pushes."; two lanes cannot hold under them, and `docs/governance.md` section 4 forbids departing from a section 7 rule by a logged decision alone, so this plan change amends the four lines in place, one line each so no cited line number moves. They now read, exactly: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` "- the runner does **one task per session**, and at most `lanes` sessions at a time (`kit/runner.json`, locked: 1 unless a logged plan change sets 2), each holding its own lane's lease; two tasks in flight never own the same file or sit in different stages, and a stage's cleanup task always runs alone (D-620);"; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:210` "- beyond the lanes, parallelism exists only inside a session, as read-only review subagents."; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:222` "- a rejected (non-fast-forward) push means another runner won, so this one exits (with two or more lanes it first tries again from a fresh read, at most twice, D-620). Git's own rule is the lock;"; and `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224` "- **nothing new is claimed on a lane while its task is `MERGE_PENDING`**, and at most `lanes` tasks are in flight; with one lane that is the old rule, one task at a time. When a task's branch falls behind `main` (another lane's merge, or Casey edited a file), the runner merges `main` into it with a normal merge commit whose tree must be exactly the reviewed work plus `main` (D-620); it never rebases and force-pushes, and a real conflict fails the attempt instead of being resolved by guesswork."; `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. Choice, stage C (active with any lane count, since a person's merge into `main` leaves a one-lane task behind too): when a MERGE_PENDING task's open pull request head is its `reviewed_sha`, its checks have not failed, and `main` is not in it, `GitHubEnv.update_branch` fetches origin's branch and goes on only while its tip is still the reviewed head (else "moved"), builds the merge commit with git plumbing (reviewed head first parent, `main` second, author and committer dated at `main`'s commit so two runners make the same commit), checks it with `UpdateMerge.is_update_merge` against `UpdateMerge.tree` before anything is pushed, and pushes it as a fast-forward (never rebased, never forced). `UpdateMerge.tree(reviewed, main)` (`runner/update_merge.py`) is `git merge-tree --write-tree` with two deterministic resolutions and no other: when both sides changed `docs/decisions.md`, its text is `main`'s file followed by the lines the branch appended after the merge base (`decisions_after_main`), whatever git's union driver did (checked with git 2.43: `merge-tree` honours `merge=union` from the working tree and puts the branch's entries first, which `check_pr_change.py`'s append-only rule fails; without the attribute it conflicts), and a branch that edited older lines or appended a D-number `main` already has is a real conflict; when both sides rewrote `kit/plan.lock` (or it conflicted) the lock is recomputed from the merged tree with the runner's own `scripts/check_plan_lock.py`, but only when each side's own lock matched its own tree, so a stale lock is never papered over and a conflicted one then stays a conflict. Any other conflicting path is a real conflict, never resolved. A pushed merge becomes the task's `reviewed_sha` and is recorded in the task's `update_merges` ({from, to, main, how, at}), so D-584's checks treat it as reviewed: `_merged`'s reviewed-head check passes on it, the unreviewed-head path never fires for it, and auto-merge stays on (GitHub keeps it across a push by a writer) or is turned on for exactly that head through `verify.auto_merge_reason`; `reviewed_plus_main` now compares a head's tree with this same `UpdateMerge.tree` of the reviewed commit and the head's `main` base, which accepts everything it accepted before plus the deterministic `docs/decisions.md` order, and rejects a union-ordered local merge. The push comes before the state record; if the record is lost, the next cycle adopts the head as reviewed when `update_merge_of` finds it is an update merge of the reviewed head (parents exactly the reviewed commit and a commit on `main`, that tree; GitHub's "Update branch" by merge qualifies too, as D-584's tree-trust idea allows), and a pull request still showing an earlier reviewed head (GitHub catching up) waits rather than failing as unreviewed; any earlier reviewed head counts as reviewed in `_head_reviewed`. A real conflict fails the attempt with the paths named (result `update_conflict`); a pull request with auto-merge on is closed first with the `DROP_MARKER` comment and recorded in `runner_closed_prs`, exactly as for an unreviewed head, and if that close fails the task stays MERGE_PENDING so any merge is judged. The retry goes through D-583's `prepare_branch`, which continues the branch with `main` merged in, or, because `main` still conflicts with it, starts fresh on `<branch>-a<n>` with the old branch kept for evidence; this plan change does not teach the worker to resolve conflicts. A rejected update push that is not a race counts toward `UPDATE_PUSH_LIMIT` (3) and then fails the attempt; a race, origin moving or a git error waits at most `UPDATE_WAIT` (2 hours, `update_waiting_since`), then fails the attempt, since a behind branch can never merge. Choice, stage D: a task in flight occupies its lane, by its live lease or, once MERGE_PENDING, by its own `lane` field written at claim (only for a lane other than "1", so a one-lane state is unchanged; `state.in_flight`), and `claim` now refuses only a lane whose own task is MERGE_PENDING (with one lane, the old rule). `runner/lanes.py` decides where a cycle may claim: at most `lanes` tasks in flight, 1 while `lanes_fallback` is set (`effective_lanes`); a run with `RUNNER_LANE` claims only that lane, a run without (routine, manual) the first free one (`claim_lane`); and beside a task in flight a candidate needs every dependency DONE or SKIPPED (no D-551 proof-waiting exception), the same stage as every task in flight, no owned path overlapping theirs (`owns`, folders covering their files; a task owning a locked file also owns `kit/plan.lock`, which it must rewrite, through `Config.locked` built from `check_plan_lock.LOCKED_FILES` and `LOCKED_GLOBS`), and neither it nor a task in flight may be a cleanup task, which runs alone (`refusal`, `compatible_ids`); FIX-MAIN is exempt, and while `main` is red `eligible` still offers nothing but FIX-MAIN on every lane. The cycle resolves every MERGE_PENDING task (`_resolve_merges`, at most one with one lane, so the result is what it was), then picks its lane; a waiting or failed result ends the cycle only when it is on the run's own lane (with one lane every task is on lane "1", so this is the old behaviour), otherwise the cycle goes on to claim, and with nothing to claim it ends with its own lane's result, else the first waiting result, else `lease_live`, else the new `no_free_lane`. `--after` and the hand-off find this session's lease on any lane (`session_lease`), the heartbeat renews the lease's own lane, and STATUS.md lists every lane's lease and a fall back. Pacing (`scripts/pacing.py`, locked) adds to `used` the estimate recorded at claim (`usage.by_task[tid].estimated_tokens`) of every other IN_PROGRESS task (`in_flight_tokens`), since a running attempt's usage reaches the ledger only at hand-in; with a quota reading this errs toward waiting; with one lane it is always 0 and the PROGRESS line is unchanged. Fall back: on a lane above 1, a rejected branch push, an attempt that could not write its review record or lease release, three lost races in one run, a required check that failed on an update merge after the same check passed on the reviewed head it started from (see the review follow-up below), and an update merge that conflicted or could not be pushed are strikes (`lane_strikes`); a task on that lane reaching DONE, or failing for its own work, clears them; the second strike in a row sets `lanes_fallback` ({at, lane, why}), writes the outbox item `lanes-fallback` (kind info) and keeps the runner on one lane, tasks in flight finishing normally, until a person runs the new `python3 -m runner --restore-lanes` (kept in `lanes_fallback_history`), so it never flaps; lane "1" never strikes. Runs: `backup-runner.yml`'s gate picks the lane a run serves (`state.run_lane`, loaded from `runner/state.py` by path as auto-pr loads `verify.py`: a dispatched `lane` input when it is a lane in use, else a lane with no task in flight, then a lane with no live lease, as the review follow-up below sets out, else lane 1); the backup job's concurrency group is per lane (`backup-runner` for lane 1, so a one-lane setup keeps its group, `backup-runner-lane-<n>` above), so two jobs run at once, one per lane, each with at most one waiting; the action and the safety hand-in get `RUNNER_LANE`; with two or more lanes the hourly tick dispatches one run per lane without a live lease and the chain step reads this job's own last report row (by session) and, after a result that moved a task, dispatches one run per lane in its `refill` (the free lanes, at most one per task that could be claimed beside the tasks in flight, pacing aside, `cycle.refill_lanes`, reported only when `lanes` is 2 or more), so a run that then claims nothing reports `idle`, `paced`, `lease_live` or `no_free_lane` and starts nothing, and the chain cannot spin; with one lane every step runs exactly as before. With two or more lanes and a handed-off worker, a lost race is tried again from a fresh read up to twice after a random 1 to 5 second wait (`cycle_with_retries`), the usual way two runs started together collide. Every state write is a compare-and-swap: `push_state` pushes `claude/kit-state` and `claude/lease` atomically and loses on any lease or state move (every push writes a new lease commit), and the writes that must survive a race (renewal, review record, branch record, release, strikes, re-queue, restore) go through `update_state`. `kit/state_schema.json` describes the task keys `lane` and `update_merges` and the top-level `lanes_fallback` and `lane_strikes`. `kit/runner.json` keeps `"lanes": 1` in this change; switching to two lanes changes only that value in code, and, since the review follow-up locks the file, is a logged plan change (see below). Two existing tests change, which `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69` allows only through a logged decision, so they are named here: `FakeEnv` in `tests/test_failure_drills.py` gains `update_branch` (default "current") and `update_merge_of` (default False), which leave every earlier drill's path as it was; and `test_lanes_setting_defaults_to_one` in `tests/test_runner_lanes.py`, whose last line pinned `kit/runner.json` to exactly 1 (D-515's stage A, when only lane "1" could be claimed), now requires the value to be the number 1 or 2, the lane counts the drills cover, so the switch needs no test change and a value that would fall back to 1 unnoticed (such as the string "2") still fails; and, in the review follow-up, `am_env` in `tests/test_runner_live.py` makes `enable_auto_merge`'s new bounded wait take no real time (the assertions are unchanged). Tests: `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` (claims on two lanes, overlap, stage, dependency and cleanup refusals, the lane-1 merge then update merge then lane-2 merge drill, a real conflict then the retry on the branch, push failures, waits, adoption, GitHub lag, red main on both lanes, the fall back and restore, pacing over both lanes, refill, the workflow's lane pick, concurrency, tick and chain snippets run as the workflow runs them), `tests/test_runner_update_merge.py` (real git: the update merge and its tree check, determinism, `docs/decisions.md` order against the union driver, reused numbers and real conflicts, an evil merge and a merge of something not on `main`, the plan lock recomputed, a stale lock and a missing lock tool left as conflicts). Review follow-up (an independent Opus review of 383a7dc found no safety hole but these gaps; all fixed in this plan change): (1) the refill never fired after a hand-in: the safety step always ran `--after` because `.git/runner_handoff.json` was never removed, and its `not_lease_holder` row became the job's last row; now `--after` removes the hand-off once it finished the task (`close_handoff`; kept for `not_lease_holder`, `lost_race` and `state_invalid`, so the safety step still frees a lease), and the chain step's refill reads the last row of this job that did something, skipping `not_lease_holder`, `renewed`, `renew_refused…` and "T### is STATUS" rows; (2) `run_lane` picked by live lease, so an event for a MERGE_PENDING lane 1 started a run that could claim nothing while lane 2 idled; it now picks a lane with no task in flight first (the event's task's lane when free, else the first free lane), then a lane with no live lease, else lane 1; (3) while `main_red` is set, an open pull request of any task but FIX-MAIN gets no update merge and no auto-merge (`merge_pending`), so the other lane cannot pile work onto a red `main`; (4) strikes now come only from attempts that ended: a failed required check strikes only when the same check passed on the reviewed head the last update merge started from (its checks are kept in `update_merges[].checks`, `_broken_by_main`), every other failed check is the task's own and clears the strikes, a rejected update push waits (`merge_pending`) and strikes only when the third one fails the attempt, and a conflict strikes because it fails the attempt; (5) finish's last write replaced the whole `usage` and `lane_strikes` on a state the other lane had moved; `_ours_onto` now lays on only this attempt's delta (the `by_task` entries it changed, the other `usage` keys it changed, its tokens added to each pacing window by `_windows_onto`, its own lane's strikes); (6) a new review record drops `update_merges`, `update_waiting_since` and `update_push_failures`, so an earlier attempt's update merges never count as reviewed heads; (7) `prepare_branch`'s merge of `main` into a retry's branch uses `UpdateMerge.tree` too, so a retry also keeps `main`'s decision entries first and a plan lock both sides kept true is recomputed; (8) `enable_auto_merge` waits up to `HEAD_POLLS` (6) times `HEAD_POLL_SECONDS` (5 s) for the pull request to show a just-pushed head before refusing, and the next cycle still retries; (9) a plan lock that needs recomputing is a real conflict when either side changed `scripts/check_plan_lock.py`, since the runner's copy of the tool cannot speak for that merge; (10) update pushes go through `push_branch`, which pushes to the explicit repository URL with `RUNNER_PUSH_TOKEN`'s credential helper (D-509; a merge of `main` may carry workflow files, which need that token's workflow scope), and the origin lookups go through `_long_token_args`; a test pins that routing; hardening: `update_merge_of` applies `reviewed_plus_main`'s fork-point rule (`_not_older_than_fork`), so an update merge onto a `main` commit older than the reviewed fork is refused. Smaller: a fall-back outbox item whose state push lost the race is removed (`_drop_fallback_note`, in the cycle's merge write, `_push_failed` and `record_strike`); while `lanes_fallback` is set the gate treats the lane count as 1 (`run_lane` and the gate snippet), so no run is started for lane 2; the chain's `again` test reads only this job's rows (by session); `runner/state.py` cites `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` and `:224`, not `:222`; `kit/runner.json` joins `scripts/check_plan_lock.py`'s `LOCKED_FILES` (and `docs/governance.md` section 1), chosen over CODEOWNERS because code-owner review is off (D-512) while the lock is enforced by `Ci` and `Governance`, so changing the lane count (or `owner_review`) needs a lock rewrite and a new decision entry, a logged plan change (main's copy of the script tolerates a file a newer list locks, D-491); and `--requeue` with two or more lanes refuses only while the task itself holds a live lease or a leased task could not run beside it (overlapping owned paths, another stage, a cleanup task on either side: `lanes.refusal` without the dependency rule), since `update_state` already makes the write itself race-safe and D-583's L2 concern was a re-queued task meeting work in flight; with one lane any live lease still refuses it. New tests for each are in `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` and `tests/test_runner_update_merge.py`. Limit kept on purpose: a refill run costs one short session even when its lane then finds nothing. Reason: the throughput Casey asked for, without two tasks ever racing for a file, a stage, a lane or the state; a branch is only ever brought up to date with exactly reviewed work plus `main`, so nothing nobody reviewed can merge; the switch is one value in a locked file, so it is logged when made, is reversible the same way, and falls back by itself before it can flap. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:210`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:222`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:246`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:509`; `docs/governance.md` section 4; D-515; D-530; D-583; D-584.

- **D-630** Question (harness plan change, October 30, 2026; the re-review of D-620 after #104 merged, before `lanes` goes to 2): three gaps. N1 (medium, blocks two lanes): a red `main` could stall the build. With `lanes_fallback` set (capacity 1), T1 IN_PROGRESS on lane 1 and T2 MERGE_PENDING on lane 2, T2's merge turns `main` red and T2 is BLOCKED; T1 hands in and becomes MERGE_PENDING, and D-620's red-main guard holds its pull request with no timeout. `in_flight` is then full, so `claim_lane` gives no lane, the cycle ends at `_stop_result` before `_red_main_step`, FIX-MAIN is never claimed and `main` stays red until someone runs `--restore-lanes`. Lowering `lanes` from 2 to 1 with two tasks in flight stalls the same way, and so does one lane when a task the guard holds is MERGE_PENDING on lane 1. N2 (low): `_windows_onto` kept the fresh window's start when this attempt's own window had rolled over, adding the old window's tokens to it, so the attempt's tokens went with a window that had already expired. N3 (low): `_head_checks` recorded a check still running at the update merge as "None", so `_broken_by_main` could never count it as passed, which made the strike rule under-sensitive. Kind: conflict for N1. D-620's `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` read "- the runner does **one task per session**, and at most `lanes` sessions at a time (`kit/runner.json`, locked: 1 unless a logged plan change sets 2), each holding its own lane's lease; two tasks in flight never own the same file or sit in different stages, and a stage's cleanup task always runs alone (D-620);" and its `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224` began "- **nothing new is claimed on a lane while its task is `MERGE_PENDING`**, and at most `lanes` tasks are in flight; with one lane that is the old rule, one task at a time."; a FIX-MAIN beyond `lanes` breaks both, so this plan change amends them in place, one line each so no cited line number moves: :209 now reads "- the runner does **one task per session**, and at most `lanes` sessions at a time (`kit/runner.json`, locked: 1 unless a logged plan change sets 2), each holding its own lane's lease, plus FIX-MAIN on the reserved fix lane when no lane can take it while `main` is red (D-630); two tasks in flight never own the same file or sit in different stages, and a stage's cleanup task always runs alone (D-620);" and :224 now begins "- **nothing new is claimed on a lane while its task is `MERGE_PENDING`**, and at most `lanes` tasks are in flight (FIX-MAIN on the fix lane aside, D-630); with one lane that is the old rule, one task at a time." (the rest of the line is unchanged); `docs/governance.md`'s enforcement row says the same, and `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. Choice, N1: of the two options, a reserved lane for FIX-MAIN or not counting guard-held tasks against capacity while `main` is red, the reserved lane is the simpler safe one: the lane already exists (D-515 reserved "fix" for FIX-MAIN; `check_state` and `free_lanes` never count it, `verify.auto_merge_reason` reads the lane named in `review_lease`, `lease.json` carries it, and `--after`, `--renew` and STATUS.md already find a lease on any lane), whereas not counting held tasks would need the lane-level MERGE_PENDING refusal in `claim`, `_stop_result` and the refill to agree on a second, red-only notion of a busy lane. `lanes.fix_lane` gives "fix" when `main` is red, FIX-MAIN can be claimed (`eligible` offers exactly it) and the fix lane holds no live lease; the cycle uses it only when `claim_lane` gives no numbered lane, so with a free lane FIX-MAIN takes that lane as before and one-lane behaviour is unchanged except in the stall itself. `state.in_flight` leaves out a FIX-MAIN on the fix lane (lease or MERGE_PENDING), so it takes no capacity, and `_lane_outcome` never strikes the fix lane. A finished FIX-MAIN must also clear `main` when every numbered lane is still held: when the cycle has no lane to claim on and `main` is red, it now runs `_red_main_step` before ending (it clears only on a green smoke run and a nightly that agrees, as before, `docs/governance.md` section 5), after which the guard lifts and the held task updates and merges. With one lane and a live lease that step does nothing new (FIX-MAIN is not DONE and the false-red withdrawal needs a FIX-MAIN not yet started), so it costs at most the check-run read `_red_main_step` already makes. Choice, N2: when a window moved on both sides, the result is the newer window by start (a window not started is the oldest); it holds the fresh tokens only when the fresh window is that window, plus this attempt's delta (all its tokens when its own window rolled over) only when its window is that window; tokens recorded in a window that has rolled over no longer count, as `pacing.windows` already treats them. Choice, N3: `_head_checks` records only finished checks, so one still running is absent rather than "None"; when a check failed on the update merge and the reviewed head's conclusion for it is absent (or the "None" a D-620 record carries), `_broken_by_main` reads that head's checks again through the new `Env.checks_on(sha)` (`GitHubEnv.checks_on`: each required check's latest run, conclusion or "running", through the job token like every check-run read, D-502; `_required_checks` is now built on it), and strikes only on a final "success"; a check still running or unreadable is not a strike. Two existing tests change, which `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69` allows only through a logged decision, so they are named here: in `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py`, `test_finish_lays_only_its_own_usage_onto_a_state_another_lane_moved` expected the rolled-over window to keep the old start with 170 tokens, the N2 bug, and now expects the newer window with only this attempt's 40; and `test_drill_red_main_holds_the_other_lanes_update_merge_and_auto_merge` expected nothing to happen with both lanes full and `main` red, the N1 stall, and now expects FIX-MAIN claimed on the fix lane while the held lanes still get no update merge or auto-merge. `FakeEnv` in `tests/test_failure_drills.py` gains `checks_on` (answers from `checks_of`, default none), which leaves every earlier drill's path as it was. Tests: drills for both N1 triggers (a fall back with a held task in the only lane, run through FIX-MAIN claimed on the fix lane, merged, `main` cleared and the held task's auto-merge turned on; and `lanes` lowered from 2 to 1 with both lanes MERGE_PENDING), the same scenario without a fall back taking lane 1 as before, the window cases, the finished-checks record, the strike re-read (passed, still running, failed, unreadable, a D-620 "None" record) and a drill that strikes on the pre-update head's final checks, and `checks_on` over a fake REST answer. Reason: a red `main` must always be fixable whatever the lane capacity, and the strike and pacing records must count what really happened. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:240`; `docs/governance.md` section 5; D-515; D-620.
- **D-646** Question (Casey, October 30, 2026: 'We are way below usage limits if we can speed it up more safely'): when does the runner start working two tasks at once? Choice: `kit/runner.json` sets `lanes` to 2, as BUILD_BRIEF.md:209 allows only through a logged plan change. Preconditions met: two lanes built and kept current by the runner (D-620), FIX-MAIN always has a lane and pacing and strike fixes are in (D-630); an independent Opus review of D-630 found it safe and ready for two lanes; RUNNER_PUSH_TOKEN has workflow scope (Casey set Contents, Workflows and Pull requests to read and write on October 29). It is switched on in daytime while Claude watches the first pairs. Rollback: the same one-line change back to 1 (tasks in flight finish normally); the runner also drops to one lane by itself after two harness-type failures in a row (D-620).

- **D-621** Question (T168, October 30, 2026): what do the security and recovery test crates hold before any task adds a case? Choice: `askhava-security` (`tests/security`, dev-dependency `trybuild` only) and `askhava-recovery-tests` (`tests/recovery`) are workspace members with no features, no dependencies on app crates yet and a `//!`-only `src/lib.rs`; each later task adds the path dependency on the app crate it exercises (reached only through its `api`) with its own driver, one `TestCases` per driver globbing only its own `ui/` cases. Both build and run with no tests under the workspace lints. Reason: SEC-029, D-488, D-597.

- **D-647** Question (T010, October 30, 2026): what exactly does the one fake-data generator (D-109) produce, and how is a sentinel kept apart from ordinary fixtures? Choice: `askhava-fixtures` (`tests/fixtures`, a workspace member with no dependencies) gives deterministic, index-based values: names cycling through seven names that are all on `scripts/pii_scan.py`'s fake-name list (the test reads the scanner's list, so the two cannot drift), E.164 phones `+1 <area> 555 0100` to `0198` under the Arizona area codes 928, 602, 480, 520 and 623 (495 distinct numbers per cycle), `person<n>@example.com` emails and `<n> Test Way` streets. The sentinels are fixed: "Zelda Canary", `+19285550199`, `canary@example.com` and "1 Canary Way" (TD-PRIV-02); the generator never yields any of them, so a sentinel found anywhere is a leak, never a fixture. - **D-677** Question (harness plan change, October 30, 2026; T233 BLOCKED after its third attempt): why did T233 fail three times when each attempt passed its own acceptance (`scripts/check_catalog.py`, `tests/test_check_catalog.py` 77 passed), and how does a task blocked by a plan bug get back? Finding: T233 edits `docs/catalog/categories.yaml`, one of the inputs of the Twin gate's license oracle; `twin/gate.py` (and `tests/twin/test_gate.py`) fail when `twin/oracle/license_scope.json` is not a fresh `twin/oracle/gen_license_scope.py` generation (D-541), so smoke, `Ci` and `Twin` were red on every attempt. The oracle sits under `twin/`, a protected path only a harness task may change (`docs/twin-warnings.md` 6.3 item 8, `runner/verify.py` `check_paths`, `scripts/check_pr_change.py` rule 1), and T233 was a build task that did not own it, so it could never pass as planned: a plan bug, not the worker's. (The "D-606" in its reason is a number reserved for T233's unmerged attempts; no D-606 is on `main`.) Regenerating the oracle on T233's pushed branch (f52cc71) changes 7 lines (the `sources` hash of categories.yaml and "paint touch-up" added to the painting grants), after which `PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python3 twin/gate.py` exits 0 (342 instances, 0 unwaived) and `tests/twin` passes (48). Other tasks checked: the oracle's inputs are `docs/catalog/categories.yaml`, `docs/catalog/license_map.yaml` and the `catalog` crosswalk in `twin/twin_config.json`; their owners are T002 (DONE), T172 and T007 (harness, DONE; T007 owns the oracle) and T233; no other task that is not DONE owns any of them (T035 owns `docs/catalog/gas_keywords.yaml`, which the oracle does not read), so T233 is the only task affected and the only one changed. Kind: conflict. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:271` read "| Checks fail | The same model gets one more try with the failure log. A Sonnet task that fails twice gets one Opus try, logged. After that the task is `BLOCKED`: dependents wait, other work continues, and it goes on the end-of-build list (§16). Casey is asked only if a human action is the only way through |" and `BUILD_BRIEF.md:540` read "- **`BLOCKED` tasks:** Claude retries with a different approach (up to 3 attempts, Opus on the last one). If one is still stuck, it stays `BLOCKED`, only its dependents wait, and it goes on the end-of-build list. It never becomes a question unless a human action is the only way through."; a task blocked by a plan bug uses its 3 attempts on a plan that cannot pass, and `--requeue` (D-583) refuses a task at the cap, so the only way back was editing `claude/kit-state` by hand, which nobody may do. Because `docs/governance.md` section 4 forbids departing from a section 7 rule by a logged decision alone, this plan change amends both lines in place, one line each so no cited line number moves: :271 now reads "| Checks fail | The same model gets one more try with the failure log. A Sonnet task that fails twice gets one Opus try, logged. After that the task is `BLOCKED`: dependents wait, other work continues, and it goes on the end-of-build list (§16), unless a logged plan change fixes the plan that made it fail: then `python3 -m runner --requeue T### --plan-fix D-###` gives it exactly one more attempt, on Opus, once per decision (D-677). Casey is asked only if a human action is the only way through |" and :540 now reads "- **`BLOCKED` tasks:** Claude retries with a different approach (up to 3 attempts, Opus on the last one). If one is still stuck, it stays `BLOCKED`, only its dependents wait, and it goes on the end-of-build list; the one exception is a plan bug: when a logged plan change (its `docs/decisions.md` entry on `main`, also listed in the task's own `decisions`) changes the task's `kit/tasks.json` entry or prompt after its last attempt started, `--requeue T### --plan-fix D-###` gives it exactly one more attempt, on Opus, once per decision (D-677). It never becomes a question unless a human action is the only way through."; `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. (D-583 and the `requeue` docstring cited the row as `BUILD_BRIEF.md:270`, which is the table's separator line; the row is :271, and the docstring now says so.) Choice, the plan (a change to `kit/tasks.json`, regenerating only `kit/prompts/T233.md` with `scripts/gen_prompts.py`'s own functions, because a full run recomputes the twin tasks' context budgets, D-520): T233 also owns `twin/oracle/license_scope.json`, for one purpose: after the categories change it runs `python3 twin/oracle/gen_license_scope.py` and commits the output unedited; it may not change the generator or anything else under `twin/`. Owning a protected path makes it a `harness` task (`scripts/validate_tasks.py`, `runner/verify.py`), so its review areas gain "harness" (it already had an Opus worker and an Opus reviewer), its file budget is 3, it lists this decision, and its acceptance adds that `gen_license_scope.py --check` and `PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python3 twin/gate.py` pass. As a harness task it may also rewrite the plan lock (`scripts/check_pr_change.py` rule 3), which it needed anyway as the owner of two locked files. Choice, the runner: `python3 -m runner --requeue T### --plan-fix D-### --reason TEXT` moves a BLOCKED task that has used all its attempts back to QUEUED for exactly one more attempt, only when, measured from the start of the task's last attempt: (a) D-### is in `docs/decisions.md` on `main` now and was not there then; (b) D-### is in the task's own `decisions` list in `kit/tasks.json` on `main` now and was not in it then (`verify.task_decisions`); and (c) the task's plan changed on `main` since then: `verify.plan_fingerprint` (sha256 of the task's `kit/tasks.json` entry as canonical JSON and its prompt file's text) differs between `main`'s commit then and `main`'s head. "Then" is the `started_at` of the task's last `history` entry, or its `ended_at` when no start was recorded (`cycle.plan_since`); `main`'s commit then is `git rev-list -1 --first-parent --before=<that time>` (`GitHubEnv.plan_evidence`). A timestamp already in the state was chosen over a hash stored at block time because it also works for tasks blocked before this change, T233 among them, and because anyone can recompute both fingerprints from git. It refuses FIX-MAIN, an unknown task, a task that is not BLOCKED, a malformed decision, a task with attempts left (plain `--requeue` covers what it may), a second plan-fix re-queue for the same decision, a task with no record of its last attempt's start or end, any lease that matters (as `--requeue`, D-583, D-620), a `main` git cannot read, and a state that moved between reading `main` and writing. It goes through `update_state`, which re-checks against the fresh state. `attempts` stays as it is, so `attempt_model` keeps the attempt on Opus and its failure blocks the task again through `record_failure` (attempts then 4); a further attempt needs another real plan change with its own new decision. The re-queue is recorded in the task's `requeues` with `plan_fix`, `plan_since`, `plan_base` and `plan_head` (`main`'s commits then and now) and both fingerprints, and "re-queued after plan fix D-###: <reason>" is appended to `last_failure`, so the attempt sees why. Plain `--requeue`'s refusal at the cap now names this way out. Tests (new; no existing test changed): `tests/test_failure_drills.py` `test_plan_fix_requeue_gives_a_capped_task_exactly_one_more_attempt`, `test_plan_fix_requeue_refuses_without_the_decision_or_a_changed_plan`, `test_plan_fix_requeue_refuses_twice_a_live_lease_and_what_plain_requeue_refuses` and `test_drill_plan_fix_requeue_runs_one_opus_attempt_and_blocks_again`; `tests/test_runner_live.py` `test_plan_fix_requeue_reads_main_at_the_last_attempts_start_and_now` (real git, dated commits on `main`) and `test_plan_fingerprint_moves_only_with_the_tasks_own_entry_or_prompt`; `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` `test_plan_fix_requeue_with_two_lanes_waits_only_for_a_lease_that_could_meet_the_task` (with `lanes` 2, as on `main` since D-646, only a live lease on the task itself or on a task that could not run beside it refuses, exactly as for `--requeue`, D-620). The number: D-646 was taken on `main` by the lanes-2 switch while this change was open, so this entry is D-677 (the live `next_decision` 657 plus 20). Amended after an independent review, before this change merged: (1) the decision must also be newly listed in the task's own `decisions`, so an unrelated decision cannot free a capped task after a change that touched its prompt only incidentally (a regeneration of every prompt, for example); since listing it changes the entry, the list check makes (c) hold as well, and (c) stays as a guard that fails closed when `kit/tasks.json` cannot be read; (2) the measure starts at the last attempt's start, not its end, so a plan fix merged while the final attempt was running (it ran on the old plan) still counts; T233 already lists D-677. Tests for the amendment: `tests/test_failure_drills.py` `test_plan_fix_requeue_needs_the_decision_newly_listed_in_the_tasks_own_decisions` and `test_plan_fix_requeue_counts_a_fix_merged_while_the_last_attempt_ran`; `tests/test_runner_live.py` `test_plan_fix_requeue_reads_main_at_the_last_attempts_start_and_now` (renamed from `test_plan_fix_requeue_reads_main_at_the_block_and_now`; a fix merged at 11:00 during an attempt that ran from 10:00 to 12:00 counts, and a decision whose commit changed the prompt but did not list it is refused) and `test_plan_evidence_reads_the_tasks_own_decisions_at_both_commits`. Documented in `docs/architecture.md` section 7 and `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` section 8. After this change merges, T233 goes back with `python3 -m runner --requeue T233 --plan-fix D-677 --reason "..."`; its next attempt continues `claude/task/T233-catalog-job-type-kinds` with `main` merged in (D-583). Reason: a task the plan made impossible must not end the build's list as a failure, a person must not edit the state by hand to free it, and the exception stays narrow and checkable: one attempt per logged, merged plan change that really changed the task. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:271`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:540`; `docs/governance.md` section 4; `docs/twin-warnings.md` 6.3 item 8; D-520; D-541; D-583; D-584; D-620.

- **D-688** Question (T011, October 30, 2026): the spec says `APP_ENV` (SEC-035, TD-SEC-13, TD-SEC-15) while `docs/architecture.md` section 5 says the parser reads only the `ASKHAVA_` prefix and refuses unknown `ASKHAVA_*` keys; which name does the app read, and how are the environments and the SEC-036 allow-lists written? Choice: the environment is `ASKHAVA_APP_ENV` (`dev`, `ci`, `test` or `live`; the spec's `APP_ENV` means this key), so one prefix rule covers every setting. The allow-lists are two settings, `ASKHAVA_ALLOW_LIST_TEST` and `ASKHAVA_ALLOW_LIST_LIVE`, each a comma-separated list of `twilio:<Account SID>`, `stripe:<account ID>`, `resend:<sending domain>` and `bucket:<bucket name>`; the identifiers are `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `ASKHAVA_STRIPE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `ASKHAVA_RESEND_DOMAIN` and `ASKHAVA_STORAGE_BUCKET`. Live needs all four identifiers and both lists, each identifier on the live list and none on the test list; test needs its own list and refuses an identifier on the live list; dev and CI only refuse an identifier on the live list (SEC-003, SEC-036). SEC-002's key check scans every `ASKHAVA_*` value for the live markers `sk_live_`, `rk_live_`, `pk_live_` outside live and the test markers in live, so a key a later task adds is covered without code; in live `ASKHAVA_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` must also start `sk_live_` or `rk_live_`. `check_base_url` (TD-SEC-13) refuses in live anything but `https://` to a non-local host; the task that adds a vendor base URL key calls it. Reason: the values are account identifiers, not secrets, but they differ per Railway project and are unknown until Casey's account checkpoint, so they are host variables rather than committed constants; a single prefix keeps the unknown-key refusal whole (D-493). Source: `docs/spec/security.md:6`, `docs/spec/security.md:40`, `docs/architecture.md` section 5.
- **D-689** Question (T011, October 30, 2026): how do the logs and Sentry keep contact data out (PRIV-016, PRIV-017, PRIV-028)? Choice: `core::api::json_layer` writes one JSON line per event with `message` and `level` at the top level (`flatten_event(true)`) and the enclosing spans under `spans`; `core::api::request_span` gives tower-http's `TraceLayer` a span with the method, the matched route template (`unmatched` for a 404) and the `x-request-id` (logged as `invalid` unless it is 1 to 64 letters, digits and dashes), never the URI; `askhava-server`'s `build_router` puts `SetRequestIdLayer`, `PropagateRequestIdLayer` and that `TraceLayer` around every route (rust-production R15), and both binaries call `start_up()` first, which parses the settings and starts logging. `Redacted<T>` prints `[redacted]` in `Debug` and `Display`, deserializes straight from the inner type and has no `Serialize`. Sentry starts only with `ASKHAVA_SENTRY_DSN`, with `send_default_pii` off, no request bodies, sentry-tracing's `ErrorLayer` at `ERROR` only (its legacy combined layer is deprecated in 0.49), and `before_send` and `before_breadcrumb` running `scrub_event`: user, request, transaction name, server name, extra data, non-system contexts, frame variables and log parameters are dropped, and every remaining text has emails and runs of seven or more phone digits replaced. Reason: names and streets cannot be detected in free text, so the type (`Redacted`) is the first wall and the scrubber the second; over-redacting a long number in an error report is the cheaper mistake. Source: `docs/spec/privacy.md:20`, `docs/spec/privacy.md:21`, `docs/spec/privacy.md:32`.
- **D-690** Question (T011 review, October 30, 2026): how are D-688's checks kept from being slipped by spelling, and how is Sentry's log path closed (SEC-032, SEC-036, PRIV-017)? Choice: live refuses to start without `ASKHAVA_ALLOW_LIST_TEST` as well as `ASKHAVA_ALLOW_LIST_LIVE`, so the foreign-account check always runs there, as D-688 states. Account identifiers are compared trimmed and lower-cased on both sides (the stored value is only trimmed), so a live identifier with a space or a case change is still refused in dev and CI. `check_base_url` reads the host after any `user:pass@`, lower-cases it, drops the port and a trailing dot, and counts `localhost` and its subdomains, any `127.` address, and IPv4 or bracketed IPv6 loopback, unspecified or IPv4-mapped loopback addresses as local. `sentry_options` sets `before_send_log` to drop every Sentry log record (the `enable_logs` switch is deprecated in sentry 0.49 and does not stop manual captures), and `scrub_event` clears the trace context's span description and data. Reason: each gap let a value the checks were meant to refuse through by a change of form only; folding case errs toward refusing. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:40`, `docs/spec/privacy.md:21`, D-688, D-689.
- **D-693** Question (T169, October 30, 2026): how does `Ci` cache, pin and install what it needs (SEC-021, SEC-045, D-453, D-481, D-488, D-491)? Choice: the Postgres service is `postgres:16@sha256:1beaa308...` (the multi-arch index digest read from the registry today; Dependabot's docker ecosystem moves it). `Swatinem/rust-cache` v2.9.3 (commit `d1527c8f`) caches the registry and `target/` (keyed by the action on `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustc) and names `target/tests/trybuild`; a step fails an exact cache hit that lacks that folder once `tests/security/ui` has cases. `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` is set for the whole workflow; `[profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only"` was already in `Cargo.toml`. cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 come from their x86_64 musl release tarballs, each checked against a SHA-256 computed from the download (the audit digest also matches the one GitHub lists). Order in `Checks`: fmt, clippy (once, workspace), `sqlx migrate run` then `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace --check -- --all-targets --all-features`, `cargo build -p askhava-server --locked`, tests, audit and deny. The migration and prepare steps run only when `migrations/*.sql` exists (none yet). The role step stays; after T012 it runs `scripts/bootstrap_roles.sql` (D-491). Every `uses:` in `ci.yml` is now a full commit SHA with its tag in a comment (checkout v4.4.0, setup-python v5.6.0, cache v4.3.0). `.github/dependabot.yml` watches `github-actions` and `docker` weekly. Brief and the audit say sqlx-cli should be a pinned prebuilt binary, but upstream publishes no sqlx-cli release binaries (the 0.9.0 release has no assets): it is built with `cargo install sqlx-cli --version 0.9.0 --locked --no-default-features --features postgres,rustls,sqlx-toml` (2 min 24 s cold, D-488) into `~/.cargo/sqlx-cli` and restored from `actions/cache` keyed on the version and toolchain; the lock-step tarball pinning does not apply. Not done here: the Playwright/e2e jobs (the task goal and owned files name only `ci.yml`, the floor file and `dependabot.yml`; `a11y.yml` belongs to another task).
- **D-694** Question (T169, October 30, 2026): how is branch coverage measured and compared, and what do the floors cover (`docs/test-design.md:39`, FEE-034, PRIV-022, LIC-033)? Choice: `ci.yml` gains a `Coverage` job that runs in parallel with `Checks`, and the job named `Ci` becomes a gate (`needs: [checks, coverage]`, `if: always()`, green only when both succeed) so the required check name is unchanged and the nightly's `needs.ci.result` still works. Coverage uses cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 (musl tarball, SHA-256 `3fca9503...`) on `nightly-2026-10-15` (rustc 1.101.0-nightly, installed and run here), `--workspace --branch` with the two trybuild drivers (`askhava-security`, `askhava-recovery-tests`) excluded because their `.stderr` files are tied to the stable rustc (D-488) and test and `bin/` files ignored. `tests/coverage_floor.json` holds `total` and `floors` keyed by path prefix: `app/payments/`, `app/catalog/src/rules.rs` (the fee rules; the catalog task changes this key with a decision if it names the fee rules in another file), `app/privacy/`, `app/licensing/`, each 95.0. A part with no branches yet is measured by its lines. A floor whose files do not exist yet is reported and not enforced; once code exists it is. The measured total today is 0.0 (35 lines in `app/server`, 0 covered, no branches; `app/core` has no code yet, contrary to the task prompt), so the total floor is 0.0 and cannot yet trip on a lost line in `app/core`; the owner of the first covered code raises it (a PR may raise a floor). The comparison is inline Python in the job (the scripts folder is locked and this task may not add to it). A PR that lowers any floor against `origin/main` fails unless its `docs/decisions.md` diff mentions the coverage floor. Shown locally: a floor of 0.5 for the total and 10.0 for `app/server/` fails with exit 1 against the measured JSON.
- **D-698** Question (T012, October 30, 2026): what does `core`'s database file hold, and how is "every GRANT is guarded, a missing role reported" shown (JOB-004, D-092, D-491)? Choice: `app/core/src/db.rs` holds `MIGRATOR = sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations")`, `app_pool(&Settings)` (lazy, `ASKHAVA_DB_POOL_MAX` connections, 5 s acquire timeout), `migrate(&SecretString)` (one connection; `DbError` names no URL or database message, only a failed migration's number) and `Guarded<T>` (`Applied(T)` / `MovedOn`, `from_returning(fetch_optional row)`, `applied()`); no extra transaction helper, `pool.begin()` is it (architecture section 5 says "a transaction helper"; section 5 is locked, so this is reported, not edited). Migration `0019` creates the `core` schema, grants `USAGE` and the default `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` with no `FOR ROLE`, preceded by a `DO` check that raises when `askhava_app` is missing; no grant is ever wrapped in `IF EXISTS`. `tests/integration/tests/migrations.rs` proves the rule for every present and future migration: each file naming `askhava_app` is run in a rolled-back transaction with the role renamed to one that does not exist and must fail naming it, and such a file may not be `-- no-transaction`; a probe wrapped in `IF EXISTS` failed the test (run here). The append-only and JOB-004 probe tables are created by the tests, not by a migration, so no test table ships. Reason: the acceptance asks for all four facts without adding production tables; the substitution test covers grants later tasks write.
- **D-699** Question (T012, October 30, 2026): what timeouts do the roles carry (postgres brain P10)? Choice: set in `scripts/bootstrap_roles.sql` with `ALTER ROLE`: `askhava_app` `statement_timeout` 15 s, `lock_timeout` 10 s, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` 30 s, `timezone` UTC; `askhava_migrator` `lock_timeout` 10 s, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` 60 s, no statement timeout. The script creates both roles `NOLOGIN` if absent (the migrator `NOINHERIT`, enforced on every run), gives `LOGIN PASSWORD` only when `ASKHAVA_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD` / `ASKHAVA_APP_PASSWORD` are in the environment (`\getenv`), grants the migrator `CONNECT, CREATE` on the database and `USAGE, CREATE` on `public`, the app `CONNECT`, revokes `CREATE` on `public` from `PUBLIC`, and with `-v test_cluster=1` adds `CREATEDB` and `GRANT askhava_app TO askhava_migrator WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE`. Ran twice here against the Ci-shaped PostgreSQL 16 (exit 0 both times), then `server migrate` as `askhava_migrator` left `core` owned by the migrator. Reason: strong_migrations' suggested values (brain P10); PG 16 has no `transaction_timeout`.
- **D-700** Question (T012, October 30, 2026): where does `server migrate` get the migration role's URL (SEC-052, D-491 deviation 5)? Choice: a new optional setting `ASKHAVA_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` (a `SecretString`); `Settings::migration_database_url()` returns `Missing` when absent, and `server migrate` (first argument `migrate` to the `server` binary) runs the normal start-up, then migrates over that URL only, never `ASKHAVA_DATABASE_URL`, and exits. The `migrate` service therefore also carries `ASKHAVA_APP_ENV` and `ASKHAVA_DATABASE_URL` for start-up. Reason: keeps the migration credential to one service and one code path; the settings parser stays the one place keys are named.
- **D-701** Question (T012 second pass, October 30, 2026, after the fresh-eyes review): how strictly is "every GRANT is guarded" proved, and what does `server migrate` report when the history disagrees with `migrations/` (JOB-004, D-491, D-698)? Choice: `every_grant_reports_a_missing_role` now also splits each migration into its top-level statements (`askhava_integration::split_statements`, which honours `--` comments, single quotes and dollar quotes), fails when a `GRANT` sits inside dollar quotes (a `DO` block or function body, where `IF EXISTS` or a `pg_roles` lookup could skip it) or a grant statement names `IF EXISTS` or `pg_roles`, and replays the file statement by statement in a rolled-back transaction, each statement naming `askhava_app` run first alone with the role renamed and required to fail naming it; `a_grant_behind_a_role_lookup_is_caught` proves the text check catches a guarded grant. The row-lock test polls `pg_stat_activity` for `wait_event_type = 'Lock'` instead of sleeping. `DbError` gains `Edited(i64)`, `Removed(i64)` and `Dirty(i64)` from sqlx's `VersionMismatch`, `VersionMissing` and `Dirty`, still with no URL or database message. Reason: the whole-file test passed as long as one statement failed, so it did not prove each grant was plain; a sleep shows only that the writer was slow, not that it waited on the lock; an operator needs the migration number to fix a refused run.
- **D-703** Question (T016, October 30, 2026): how does `adapters` pick stand-in, sandbox or live, where do its Twilio settings live, and how is the fixed masked pool given (SEC-002, SEC-018, SEC-032, CALL-017, D-160, D-493)? Choice: `askhava_adapters::api::TwilioConfig::from_settings` reads seven new keys from the same pairs `Settings::from_pairs` takes (the names are added to `KEYS` in `app/core/src/settings.rs`, so startup still refuses an unknown key, but the typed values live in `adapters`, because `core` is layer 0 and cannot name adapter types): `ASKHAVA_ADAPTER_MODE_TWILIO` (`stand_in`, `sandbox`, `live`; default `live` in live and `stand_in` elsewhere; `live` outside live is `LiveKeyOutsideLive`, `stand_in` in live is `StandInInLive`), `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_BASE_URL` and `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_VERIFY_BASE_URL` (override the mode's defaults, `http://127.0.0.1:4010/twilio` for the stand-in and `https://api.twilio.com` and `https://verify.twilio.com` otherwise, each through `check_base_url`), `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` (a secret), `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID`, `ASKHAVA_MASKED_POOL_SIZE` (default 10, D-160) and `ASKHAVA_MASKED_NUMBERS` (required: exactly the pool size of distinct E.164 numbers). The account SID still comes from `Settings::account(Vendor::Twilio)`, already on its allow-list. The voice adapter dials only from a `PoolNumber`, which only the settings list makes, and has no number-buying method. `IdempotencyKey::derive(secret, action, ids)` is HMAC-SHA256 over the length-prefixed action and record IDs, 64 hex digits; the caller passes `ID_SECRET`, which is not yet a setting, so the task that adds `ASKHAVA_ID_SECRET` wires it. Every POST sends the key as `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Askhava-Message-Key` (the stand-in's sent-log key, OPS-017). Verify's `check_code` takes no key (`check_` is a read-only prefix, D-596). Twilio ignores `Idempotency-Key`, so for Twilio the derived key is a sent-log marker only; duplicate protection comes from the caller's outbox checking the sent log for the key before any resend. `AdapterError` splits a failed call into `NotSent` (the client could not be built or could not connect, reqwest `is_builder`/`is_connect`: safe to resend) and `OutcomeUnknown` (anything after sending: check the sent log first). `ASKHAVA_ADAPTER_MODE_TWILIO=sandbox` in live is `TestKeyInLive` (SEC-002: no test key in live). The HTTP client follows no redirects, so the Basic-auth credentials never go to another host. The HTTP tests start `python3 -m stand_ins.server` on a free port from the repository root. Reason: the base URL stays the only difference between stand-in, sandbox and live (D-453); a fixed list sized by settings is CALL-017's "the app never buys numbers itself"; the budget was 8 files, and this needed the crate's `api.rs`, `tests/mod.rs` and `CLAUDE.md` besides (shared paths), so the overrun is in shared files only; the change is also about 1,090 lines against the 350-line budget, mostly the HTTP and settings tests and the config parsing, which the three clients and the checked config need.
- **D-723** Question (harness plan change, October 30, 2026; after D-620 and D-630, with `lanes` at 2): how is a lane whose task merged, or which is free, always picked up within minutes, even when GitHub drops a waiting run? What happened (read from the runs and `kit/runner_log.jsonl` on `claude/kit-state`): T169 was MERGE_PENDING on lane 2 and its pull request #114 merged at 13:59:51Z. Run 41066868733 (lane 1) had claimed T012 at 13:59:37, before that merge, so its cycle could not resolve T169, and its lease reached `claude/lease` only at 14:03, so both gates that read it at 14:00 saw lane 1 as free. The `pull_request` run 41067932795 and the `ci` run 41067949272 both picked lane 1 (`run_lane`: T169's lane 2 was busy with its MERGE_PENDING task, lane 1 looked free), both queued in lane 1's group `backup-runner` behind T012's running job, and GitHub, which keeps one waiting job per group, cancelled the older one's `backup` job. Run 41067949272 started at 14:26:27, after T012 handed in, resolved T169 (MERGE_PENDING to DONE) at 14:28:05 and reported `merge_pending` (T012 now waiting on lane 1) with `refill: ["2"]`, but the chain step refills only after a result in its moved list, and `merge_pending` is not in it, so it printed "chain: no" and started nothing. Lane 2 sat idle until a person dispatched `-f lane=2` at 14:30. So the root cause is two gaps, not the cancellation itself: a merged pull request's run was sent to a lane that only looked free, and a run that freed another lane did not refill it because its own lane's result was a wait; a third gap made the same idle time likely after any claim: refill runs start only when a job ends, and a job that hands off ends only after its worker's whole session. A dropped waiting run is otherwise harmless, since the newer run that replaced it serves the same lane. Kind: gap; no section 7 line changes, `kit/plan.lock` is written and unchanged (no locked file changes), and `.github/` and `runner/` change only in this logged plan change. Options weighed: (a) a check of every lane at the end of every run against the Actions API's queued and running runs and their lane inputs: the runs API does not return dispatch inputs and the lane of an event run is known only after its gate, so it needs a run name or job name per lane and paginated reads, and it still acts only when a job ends; (b) a 15-minute tick: every tick starts a Claude session per lane with no live lease, including lanes that are only waiting on checks, which costs sessions without fixing the routing; (c) the resolving run dispatching the freed lane: it already reports the lane in `refill`, so the fix there is one condition. Choice, three small changes, each bounded: (1) the gate passes `MERGED` (`github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, which the gate's `if` limits to a pull request merged into `main`) to `run_lane`, which then serves the event's task's own lane whenever it is a lane in use and holds no live lease; that lane's run resolves the merge and can claim there at once, and every other event still prefers a lane with no task in flight first (D-630 review follow-up 2); a dispatched `lane` still wins, and with one lane or a fall back the answer is lane 1 as before. (2) The chain step's refill also fires when the job's last row that did something has a non-empty `changed.tasks`, so a run whose own lane still waits but which resolved another lane's merge starts a run for each lane in its `refill`. (3) A cycle that hands off starts its refill runs itself at once (`start_refill` in `runner/__main__.py`, after `refill` is worked out and before the log row is written, which now also carries `dispatched`): `GitHubEnv.dispatch_lane` runs `gh workflow run backup-runner.yml --ref main --repo <repo> -f lane=<n>` with the job token, as the chain step does; `_job_token_call` routes exactly that command to `RUNNER_CHECKS_TOKEN` (the job token has `actions: write`) and never to the long-lived `RUNNER_PUSH_TOKEN`, and without the job token (a routine or local run), in a dry run or for a lane that is not a number nothing is started; a failed start is logged (token-like text redacted) and never changes the result. Only `handed_off` starts runs from the runner: every other result ends its job within minutes and the chain step refills. No storms and no loops: `refill` lists only free lanes, at most one per task that could be claimed beside the tasks in flight, and never this run's own lane (its new lease holds it); a started run that claims nothing reports `idle`, `paced`, `lease_live` or `no_free_lane` with no task moved, which starts nothing; and GitHub keeps at most one waiting job per lane group, so a second start for a lane replaces the waiting one instead of adding to it. With `"lanes": 1` `refill` is never worked out, nothing is dispatched from the runner, `run_lane` answers lane 1 and every step runs as before. The hourly tick stays the last net for an event GitHub never delivers. No existing test assertion changes; the `_pick` helper in `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` gains an optional trailing argument for `MERGED` (calls without it run the snippet exactly as before). Tests (`tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py`): `run_lane` on the incident's state (lane 1 for a `ci` event, lane 2 for the merged pull request, lane 1 with one lane, a fall back, no task, an unknown task or a live lease on the task's lane); the gate's lane-pick snippet run as the workflow runs it with `MERGED` true, false and absent, and the step's env and argument; the chain step's refill snippet over the 14:28 row (refills lane 2) and over rows with no task moved or from another job (nothing); `start_refill` (one start per lane, a failed and a raising start skipped); `main` starting refill runs only after `handed_off` with two lanes and not in a dry run; and `dispatch_lane` (the exact command, the job token, never the long-lived token, only the runner's own workflow, no token, dry run, a failure logged with the token redacted). Review follow-up (an independent review found nothing blocking; all fixed in this plan change): (1) `MERGED` is `github.event.pull_request.merged == true`, not `github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so a closed pull request that did not merge (such as one the runner closed) is never treated as freeing its lane, even if the gate's own `if` changes; (2) the gate's lane pick calls `run_lane` with `merged` and, on a `TypeError` from a checkout whose `runner/state.py` predates it, calls it again without, instead of failing to the silent "1 1 -" fallback; (3) `refill_lanes` names no lane while the pacer's last decision is a wait whose `waiting_until` is still ahead (`_pacer_waiting`; an unreadable or missing time does not count), so a paced period starts no empty runs from the hand-off or the chain step. Tests: the expression, the lane pick over a stand-in `state.py` without `merged`, and refill under a pending, an expired, an unreadable and no wait. Reason: a second lane is worth its cost only if it never idles behind the other lane's session; the cheapest exact signal of a free lane is the `refill` the runner already computes, and the merged pull request's own event is the earliest moment its lane is known to free up. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:213`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:260`; D-500; D-502; D-620; D-630.
- **D-708** Question (T013, October 30, 2026): how is the `core.task` queue and its worker built from the second trial (JOB-006, D-491), and where does the loop live? Choice: `core.task` (`migrations/0020_core_task_queue.sql`) has kind, IDs-only `jsonb` payload, `run_at`, `attempts`/`max_attempts` (default 5), `lease_owner` uuid and `lease_until` (both null or both set, a check), `last_error`, `done_at`, `dead_at`, a unique `dedupe_key`, the partial index `(run_at) WHERE done_at IS NULL AND dead_at IS NULL` and `autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.02` (postgres brain P9). `app/core/src/tasks.rs` holds the trial's SQL as literal macros: `enqueue` (`ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id`, over a `&mut PgConnection` so it joins the caller's transaction, R11; a generic executor would trip the `Executor` scan of TD-SEC-10), `claim` (`UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … attempts < max_attempts AND (lease_until IS NULL OR lease_until < now) ORDER BY run_at, id LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)`, raising `attempts`), `finish`, `renew` and `fail`, `release_leases` (gives the attempt back: a release happens only on a clean shutdown, so a task a deploy interrupted is not charged an attempt and a task cannot be dead-lettered by deploys alone; the consequence is that a handler aborted after the 20 s drain may already have done part of its work and runs again in full, which the JOB-006 re-check and the derived idempotency key make safe, and a handler that outlasts the drain on every deploy is never dead-lettered by its attempts, only stopped by its 2-minute timeout between deploys) and `reap_expired` (dead-letters a lease that ran out on the last attempt). Every "now" is passed in from the injected clock and every lease end is computed in Rust. One change from the trial: `finish`, `renew` and `fail` are fenced by lease owner *and* the claim's attempt number, since one worker process's lanes share an owner ID and the owner alone would let a lane finish a task another lane of the same process had reclaimed. Backoff is 30 s doubled per failed attempt, at most an hour; `HandlerError` holds a `&'static str`; the fixed sentences are `NO_HANDLER`, `TIMED_OUT`, `LEASE_EXPIRED`. `Registry::run` runs one claimed task (lease renewed at half-life, 2-minute timeout, then the fenced finish or fail), so the tests drive the same path the worker does. The loop is `Worker::run` in `app/core/src/tasks.rs`, started by `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` (D-710): 4 at once in a `JoinSet`, idle poll 200 ms doubling to 5 s, the reaper on an idle poll, finished runs collected with `try_join_next` before each claim so finished-but-uncollected runs never hold a slot, a failed claim, reap or renew logged once with a fixed sentence (rust brain R5), and on SIGINT or SIGTERM stop claiming, 20 s drain, abort, `release_leases`, exit 0 (rust brain R14). The 20 s drain is not checked against Railway's grace period (**verify with host**). `WorkerId` comes from the database's `gen_random_uuid()`, so no `uuid` feature or `rand` is needed. `core` now names `jiff-sqlx` (with its `postgres` feature, which the workspace pin does not turn on), `serde_json` and `tokio` as normal dependencies; all three are already on the allow-list and in `Cargo.lock`, so no new crate. `docs/architecture.md` section 5 already describes this design and was left alone (it is locked); section 2's worker line is updated. Reason: the trial's measured shape (D-491), with the per-claim fence closing the one gap it left. Size: the prompt's budget is 4 files and 450 changed lines; T013 changed its 4 owned files plus shared paths (`api.rs`, the two `lib.rs`, the two crate `CLAUDE.md` files, the `core` and integration `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `settings.rs`, `worker.rs`, `.sqlx/`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`, this file), so the file overrun is in shared files only, and it is about 1,700 changed lines, mostly the integration tests (TD-SEC-19 and the queue tests the prompt names), the queue and rate-limit code and the generated `.sqlx/` query files; kept as one change because the queue, its loop and its tests only work together.
- **D-709** Question (T013, October 30, 2026): how are the rate-limit counters and the client IP built (SEC-040, SEC-014, SEC-053)? Choice: `core.rate_limit` (bucket, fixed `window_start`, `hits`; primary key on the first two) raised by one `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (bucket, window_start) DO UPDATE SET hits = hits + 1 RETURNING hits`; a request is allowed while the count is at most the limit (`rate_limit::hit`, re-exported as `rate_limit_hit`); `prune` deletes old windows. A bucket is a scope plus an IP (`ip_bucket`) or a blind-index hash; never a plaintext contact value (P12). `ClientIpPolicy::from_pairs` reads two new optional keys from the same pairs `Settings::from_pairs` takes, added to `KEYS` the way D-703 did: `ASKHAVA_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (default `x-real-ip`, taken to be the header Railway's edge sets but not checked in this session; **verify with host** on the test project and record in `docs/deploy.md`, OPS-050) and `ASKHAVA_PROXIED_HOSTS` (empty at launch, SEC-053). `client_ip` takes the edge header's address, the socket peer when the edge sent none (a missing edge header puts everyone in one bucket, the stricter failure), and `CF-Connecting-IP` only when the `Host` is a proxied hostname and the edge address is in `CLOUDFLARE_RANGES`; `X-Forwarded-For` is never read. The Cloudflare ranges are a constant written from Cloudflare's published list as known to this session and not fetched here, so they must be re-checked against https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/ in the decision that first proxies a hostname. No case went into `app/core/src/tests/settings.rs` (not this task's file); the two keys are tested through `ClientIpPolicy` in `tests/integration/tests/task_queue.rs`. TD-SEC-19's passkey sign-in case belongs to the owner sign-in task; this task covers the 5-of-20 count, the spoofed `X-Forwarded-For`, the named header and the Cloudflare rules. `prune` (`prune_rate_limits`) has no caller yet: the task that first adds a nightly job registers it, until then old windows only take space. Reason: SEC-040 as written; the setting pattern of D-703 keeps `Settings` unchanged for other tasks. Size: counted with D-708 (one change over the 450-line budget).
- **D-710** Question (T013 review, October 30, 2026): the reviewer found the worker's claim loop untested, because it lived in the `worker` binary, which a test cannot import, and found that `JoinSet::len` counts finished runs nobody collected, so the loop could fall to one task at a time. D-491 put the claim loop in the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs`. Choice: the loop moves into `core` as `Worker::run(shutdown, drain)` in `app/core/src/tasks.rs` (with `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` and the poll bounds), the shape the second trial had (`app/core/src/worker.rs` there, `docs/audit/rust-trial-2-2026-10-29.md`); `worker.rs` still owns the process: settings, pool, `WorkerId`, `register_handlers()`, the signal and the 20 s `DRAIN`, and is now the only place that starts the loop. Before each claim the loop collects finished runs with `try_join_next`.
