- **D-1018** Question (T184): when does "also send me jobs nobody else covers" apply (CARD-004, TD-LIC-03 "if one business ticked it, overflow doesn't apply"), and how do the pauses reach matching (CARD-016)? Choice: `quotes::api::rules::match_job` first runs the CARD-001 checklist match under the owner pauses; only when that reaches nobody does the card go to every business with the switch on (`Pooled::overflow_on`, read from `businesses::api::Business::overflow_on`) that passes every CARD-001 check except the ticks (`card_under(.., (business, true))`): active, verified, serving an Arizona offer town, licensed for every candidate. On a job's first send, a business that ticked the job type but cannot receive it (paused, unlicensed for a candidate) does not block overflow; on a rerun (`send_job_cards`, `send_late_cards`) `rules::match_job_held` is given the job's card holders, and a holder whose checklist covers the job (verified, serving an offer town, licensed, ticking a candidate, whatever its status or the pauses now) keeps overflow off, so a job a ticked business already covered never gets overflow cards later (TD-LIC-03, review fix). The result therefore depends on the order of events, and the decided reading is CARD-004 judged at each send against the businesses able to receive it then, with cards never withdrawn: (a) a ticked business T paused (or under an owner pause) at the first send does not block overflow, so the switch-on businesses get overflow cards and keep them; when T is unpaused while the job is Open or No quotes yet, the rerun's checklist match reaches T, T gets its own late card (CARD-018) and no further overflow card goes out, so the job ends with both; (b) T able to receive at the first send gets the card and overflow never applies to that job, even if T is paused later and a switch-on business becomes eligible (second review). The business pause is the existing `AccountStatus::receives_cards`; the owner switches (OPS-003) come in as `OwnerPauses` (the "all" switch, paused category codes, paused town codes), which the caller fills through `ops::api::is_paused`, mapping each town or trade switch's record ID to its code; a business is skipped (`Skip::OwnerPaused`, checked first) under "all", when a candidate's trade is paused, when the job's own town (the first offer town) is paused, or when every offer town it serves is paused: a paused town takes no new jobs, so pausing the job's town stops every business for that job even one also serving a neighbouring town, while a paused neighbouring town only stops a business that serves no unpaused offer town (review fix; CARD-016's "its town" read as the job's town as well as the business's). `CardBusiness` and `CardJob` are unchanged (T044's tests build them by literal), so the switch rides on the new `Pooled` wrapper and the pauses on `Pool`. Reason: CARD-004 is a fallback for a job no checklist reaches, and keeping the T044 records stable keeps its tests untouched.
- **D-1019** Question (T184): how are INT-017's N and INT-032's SPLIT offer decided? Choice: `quotes::api::coverage(job, pool)` (the shipped license map; `rules::coverage` is the pure form) returns `Coverage::Send(n)` with n the number `match_job` reaches now (overflow included, so N is what CARD-001 and CARD-004 would send); with none, `Coverage::Split` when the candidates span two or more categories and the candidates of at least one category alone reach a business, else `Coverage::NotCovered`. SPLIT is never offered when some active, verified business serving an offer town is licensed for every candidate job type (ticks, the overflow switch and owner pauses aside): then no license fails to cover the job, INT-032's condition does not hold, and the reply is Not covered (a business licensed for plumbing and electrical that ticked neither, with a plumbing-only business ticking plumbing, gets Not covered, not SPLIT; `td_int_25_no_split_when_one_business_is_licensed_for_every_trade`, second review). SPLIT is offered only when splitting would get at least one part sent; the other part, if nobody covers it either, gets its own Not covered on its own pass. Reason: INT-032's offer is only useful when a split request can be sent; INT-017's not-covered reply covers the rest.
- **D-1020** Question (T184): how does intake use the coverage, and what are "two requests" after SPLIT? Choice: `intake::api::tell_coverage(db, secret, (request, coverage, job), routing)` queues `coverage_count_many` ("Ask Hava: Got it. We'll send this to the {count} {trade} businesses on Ask Hava."), `coverage_count_one` (the singular) or `split_offer` (the INT-032 words), all exactly the spec text, with Spanish drafts (DIVIDIR) in `es.json`; `tell_coverage` takes the job it is told about; a job already final, like a closed request, gets no count line or SPLIT offer (second review); `Coverage::NotCovered` moves only that job to Not covered (reply, demand row, audit row, one transaction) while another job of the request is still live (not final), so after a SPLIT an uncovered second trade never touches the first trade's job and the request stays open (review fix); with no other live job it runs `apply` with the new `Why::NobodyCovers`, so the request moves from Intake to Not covered and, like a trade that is not open, gets a recruiting-demand row (recruiting can fill it, unlike LIC-017 and LIC-018's refusals, D-1008). A closed request gets nothing. `split_request` takes a reply of SPLIT or DIVIDIR alone (`is_split_reply`) and opens the second trade's job through `conversation::begin_job` (the one job-opening path, given the request's own description), so each trade is a job matched and sent alone (D-993 keeps a request's jobs as answer rows); the caller then matches the first job with its own trade's candidates only. `split_request` trusts its caller and does not check that a SPLIT offer was made; the conversation wiring must call it only for the reply to a `Coverage::Split` offer of the same request (documented on the function and in `app/intake/CLAUDE.md`, second review). Wiring these into the conversation is the conversation task's, like the rest of routing (D-1008). `Outcome` and `Request` keep their shape because T043's tests match and build them. Reason: INT-017, INT-032, D-435, D-482.
- **D-1021** Question (T184): CARD-018's late card needs the job's status, and the change runs past the 250-line budget. Choice: `quotes::api::send_late_cards` reads the job through `jobs::api::current` and asks the new `JobStatus::takes_late_cards` (Open or No quotes yet; a shared `status.rs` method, so no status is compared outside it, SEC-031); it records a card only for businesses holding none, sent now, so each late card's 24 hours start then (D-042). `sent_at` is the `now` passed in, exactly as T044's `send_cards` records it; the quiet-hours hold (QH rules, D-042's "after any quiet-hours hold") is applied by the card delivery step, not here, so a late card found at night is recorded now and held by delivery like any first card (second review). The status read and the card inserts run in one transaction; the insert cannot be made conditional on the job's status in SQL without `quotes` naming the `jobs` schema (R8) or a row-lock call `jobs::api` does not offer, so a move committed between the read and the insert is accepted: the mover never reads `quotes.job_card`, so the result equals a card sent just before the move (a limit, review fix). What makes a business newly eligible (activation, unpause, a new tick) is an event in lower crates, which cannot call `quotes`; the handler that reruns `send_late_cards` for the business's Open and No quotes yet jobs is the worker wiring's, not built here. `quotes` gains `askhava-jobs` and `intake` gains `askhava-quotes` (both allowed by `kit/layers.json`), and the workspace `Cargo.toml` gains its `askhava-quotes` entry. The owned files change by about 960 lines (rustfmt-formatted), over the 250-line budget: about 615 are the two test files and most of the rest is documentation, which must land with the rules they guard. Reason: CARD-018, D-042, D-481.

Choice: `quotes::api::build_card(&CardParts, min_words)` is the only way to make a `JobCard`, whose private fields are the town, the kind of place, the screened card-photo IDs (CARD-013, CARD-014; the concept image's ID joins them, INT-046) and the gated text; `CardParts` has no field for a name, phone, email, street address, on-site contact or original photo. The kind of place is a closed enum of CARD-006's four examples (`Place::House`, `Marina`, `StorageLot`, `Ramp`); a new kind is a new variant when the intake question that asks it is built. The "How soon?" answer is `Timing` (INT-030's four answers, "Needed by <day>" for 4) and the 911 line is `Danger`, CARD-007's five fixed words, so a card can never carry her safety wording or a gas-company question (D-436, TD-CARD-08). CARD-009's 5 is a parameter with `DEFAULT_MIN_WORDS` = 5; the caller passes the setting, and adding the `ASKHAVA_*` key is left to the task that wires card sending, since nothing reads it yet. - **D-1025** Question (T045): what exactly does CARD-008's "anything shaped like a name, a contact phrase, a run of number words or 7 or more digits" match, and what is "the rest of that sentence"? Choice: `quotes::api::final_gate` works line by line (each card field is its own line) and splits a line into sentences after `!`, `?` or a `.` followed by a space, but not after a digit (so "928. 555. 0100" stays one run), a single letter, a title (Mr, Mrs, Ms, Dr, Sr, Sra) or a street direction (N, S, E, W, NE, NW, SE, SW, so "1234 N. Example Dr" stays one sentence). In each sentence the first matching word and every word after it go, and a kept prefix ends with a full stop. Name shapes: "ask for", "talk to", "speak to/with", "meet", "pregunte por" before any word, skipping "a/an/the/some", that is not an everyday word ("ask for a quote" stays, "ask for the owner Pat" goes); "I'm", "im", "I am", "this is" before any word not on a common-word list ("I'm worried" stays, "im pat" goes); "it's" or a title before a capitalised word other than "I"; "my"/"our"/"mi" before a contact or on-site person word (number, cell, phone, email, address, owner, manager, tenant, husband, wife, son, daughter, neighbor, roommate, landlord, caretaker). Contact phrases: "call/text/email/reach/message/dm/ring" before "me", "us", an on-site person word or a capitalised word ("Text Pat"), "contact", "my name", "name is", "phone number", "cell number", "whatsapp", "me llamo", "llame". Also: any word with `@`, links, any domain-shaped word (2 or more letters or digits, a dot, 2 or more letters: "pat.lee", "example.com/pat"; not "a.m." or "3.5"), "<word> at <domain>", "<word> at <word> dot <word>", a 1-to-6-digit number with a street word within the next 4 words, a 3-to-6-digit number before a capitalised word ("unit 1234 Kiowa"), the letter O counted as a zero inside a digit group ("555 O142"), 3 number words in a row (English or Spanish, hyphenated compounds counted per part), and 7 or more digits and number words in a run of digit groups however spaced or punctuated. The gate errs toward removing words (a "2 doors on the way" sentence loses its tail), because the description fallback (CARD-009) and the job page (CARD-023) keep the job readable. The gate repeats its pass until nothing changes (a cut can leave a new shape, as "lot 3." before "Drive"), so its output is a fixed point: gating it again changes nothing, which TD-CARD-11's equality and CARD-009's count rely on; `build_card` counts the 5 words on that fixed point, so the description counted is the one stored. Known limits: a name with no cue, title, contact verb or capital after a self-introduction ("Pat will open the gate") is not caught; that is left to the scrubber (AI-002). The CARD-010 restricted-word list is not part of this task. Reason: CARD-008 names shapes, not a pattern list; this is the smallest plain-code reading that removes every TD-CARD-01 shape and the twin's oversharer texts (`twin/twin.py`) while keeping ordinary job words.

- **D-1036** Question (plan change, October 31, 2026; Casey approved it in chat: re-measure the context budgets and set the limit where the real tasks sit; numbered D-1036 because PR #191 took D-1030 and the runner's next claim (T185) takes the block starting at max(`next_decision`, main's highest + 1) = D-1031, so D-1031 to D-1035 (`DECISION_BLOCK` 5, `runner/state.py:49`) are left for it; the unused D-1028 and any gap are harmless, and the approved follow-up change will make plan changes draw from the runner's counter so this guesswork ends): the stored `budget.context_pct` values no longer describe the tasks, and most real tasks are over the 20% limit; what should be counted and where should the limits sit? Finding (measured on `main` at 02abd6c with `main`'s own `scripts/gen_prompts.py`): 202 of the 221 prompts measure over 20% and 214 differ from their stored value (stored values run from equal to about 20 times too low; the stored maximum is 24); build, docs and audit tasks reach 39 (T038, T039) with a median of 23; `docs/architecture.md` (141,485 bytes, about 35k tokens, 17.7% of the window) is read by 207 tasks and is the largest single term. Eight harness tasks measure over 30: T167 32, T169 34, T170 45, T172 48, the queued T074 78 (it reads the whole `twin/` directory, 299,648 bytes, while owning two files in it, so `twin/app.py` and `twin/gate.py` counted twice) and the finished twin tasks T005 87, T006 89, T007 101. The cleanup tasks that own `app/` and `migrations/` as directories (T057, T075, T100, T142, T126) measure 224 to 262, because the whole tree (about 1.6 MB) counted as loaded; no limit fits them. The 20% limit comes from D-485 (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:190` before this change) and compares only the stored value (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:401`); the runner never reads `context_pct` (nothing under `runner/` names it); it reaches the worker only as the prompt line "at most N% of the context window" (`kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:33`). D-1023 left T184's budget stale for that reason ("refreshing it belongs to whatever change re-measures the whole plan"), and D-1029 re-rendered every prompt with the stored values. Kind: plan hygiene (harness tooling and `kit/tasks.json`). Choice: (1) `context_bytes` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:432`) counts an owned path only when it is a regular file that exists: an owned directory counts nothing (a cleanup task greps and sweeps a tree, it does not load it). A read that names an owned file is skipped, and a directory read leaves out the owned files it holds (`read_bytes`, `scripts/gen_prompts.py:447`), so nothing counts twice; a directory read still counts the rest of the tree, which the worker does read. (2) The limits (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:192` to `:202`, chosen by `context_limit`, `scripts/validate_tasks.py:379`): 45 for build, docs and audit (measured max 39), 50 for harness (the largest live harness task is T074 at 41 after step 3; T172, done, 48), and a new 65 for cleanup (T126 measures 59 because it reads the whole twin for its chaos run, which its acceptance line needs; the four other `app/` sweeps measure 22, T008 30). The finished twin tasks T005, T006 and T007 still measure 63, 65 and 69 (they edited `twin/app.py` and `twin/twin.py`, 190 KB, whole); they are listed in `CONTEXT_LIMIT_HISTORY` under a limit of 75 (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:201`) so their stored numbers stay honest instead of trimmed; no other task may use it. (3) T074 (QUEUED) no longer reads `twin/`: it owns `twin/app.py` and `twin/gate.py`, already counted, and its goal names its other inputs (the rules modules in `app/`, `.github/workflows/twin.yml`, the schema); `twin/twin.py` and `twin/vendors.py` call `app.py` but T074 changes how the gate reaches the rules, not the simulation, so no other twin file is listed. T074 measures 41 (was 78). (4) `gen_prompts.py --check --strict` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:498`, `:548`) fails on any stored value that differs from the measurement. Plain `--check` (Ci, `scripts/smoke.sh:71`, `tests/test_gen_prompts.py`'s real-prompts test) still prints drift as a note, not a failure: measured on the last five task merges to `main` (T040, T042, T183, T044, T184), each moved 16 to 41 tasks' measurements by a point or more (every merge grows `docs/architecture.md` and adds owned files), and a task branch may not rewrite `kit/tasks.json`, so a strict Ci check would make every later task fail Ci until a plan change refreshed the numbers. Instead the plan-change routine runs `--strict` before it commits (`docs/ai-operating-manual.md:87`), so every plan change leaves the numbers honest. (5) Every stored `budget.context_pct` is re-derived by a full `python3 scripts/gen_prompts.py` run (`derive_context`, `scripts/gen_prompts.py:463`), and every prompt is re-rendered with D-1029's append-at-end sentence kept. After it, every build task is at most 39, docs 21, audit 25, cleanup 59, harness 48 (T005 to T007 63, 65, 69), `--check --strict` reports 0 problems and `scripts/validate_tasks.py` 0 errors. Tests: `tests/test_gen_prompts.py:328` (strict fails a stale budget and passes after regeneration; plain `--check` still passes) and `:346` (owned directory counts nothing; owned file counted once through a file read and a directory read; an owned directory that is also read counts as a read); `tests/test_validate_tasks.py:598` (45, 50 and 65 each pass at the limit and fail one above, by type) and `:614` (only T005 to T007 get 75); `tests/test_validate_tasks.py:350` and `:587` now use the new limits (one over each). `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. Reason: the 20% limit was set before the prompts pasted their sources and before `docs/architecture.md` grew; a limit every task breaks guides nobody, and a stored number that is wrong by a factor of two tells a worker nothing true. - **D-1031** Question (T185, CARD-010, TD-CARD-02): how does the final gate remove carrier-restricted phrases and log them without the text? Choice: each pass of `quotes::gate::final_gate` runs the CARD-008 contact cut on each sentence and then `strip_restricted` per line over `catalog::api::RESTRICTED_WORDS` (read through `catalog::api`, D-492), matching whole words of letters and digits in any case as `catalog::api::restricted_match` does, longest phrase first and never twice over the same words, so "neo-Nazi" is one removal of "neo nazi"; the words are cut, punctuation left on its own is dropped (a sentence's last stop moves to the word before), and each removal logs `tracing::info!(entry, ...)` with only the list entry (D-485). A line with no listed phrase is returned unchanged, and the gate's fixed-point loop also removes a phrase another removal joined up. The contact cut comes first because the list matches runs of letters and digits, so removing "beer" first would turn the domain "joes.beer.biz" into "joes..biz", which the domain shape no longer sees (PRIV-006); cut first, the domain goes whole. A fragment ending in a hyphen that a removal leaves ("e-" from "e-cigarette") is dropped with the stray punctuation. `askhava-catalog` moves from a dev-dependency to a dependency of `askhava-quotes` and `tracing` (already a workspace crate) joins it; `kit/layers.json` already lets `quotes` call `catalog`, and no new crate enters the workspace. Reason: CARD-010, D-485, D-492, D-813 (trade words kept off the list stay untouched). Source: `docs/spec/job-cards.md:14`, `app/catalog/src/restricted_words.rs:93`.
- **D-1032** Question (T185, CARD-019): what does the card say when N is 1? CARD-019 writes the line as "Sent to <N> businesses."; for one business that reads "Sent to 1 businesses.". Choice: "Sent to 1 business." for N = 1 and "Sent to <N> businesses." for every other N, with no cap; the meaning is CARD-019's. The Spanish line ends with a full stop like the card's other sent lines ("Homeowner prefers Spanish."), as the cold read and the copy panel suggested; the cold read's "Only sent to you." for N = 1 is not taken, because N is the provider-accepted count the caller passes and late cards can raise it (CARD-018). Kind: wording. Reason: `docs/voice.md` (plain words, as a neighbour says it); D-188, WORD-028, WORD-029. Source: `docs/spec/job-cards.md:16`, `docs/spec/job-cards.md:23`.
- **D-1033** Question (T185, CARD-012, CARD-019, FEE-045, TD-CARD-03, TD-CARD-07): where do the Spanish, fee-free and "Sent to <N> businesses." lines live, given the stored card text is the same for every business (TD-CARD-11) but the Spanish line depends on the business and N on send time? Choice: `quotes::api::CardLines` (`sent_to`, `prefers_spanish`, `fee_free`) and `JobCard::text_for(&CardLines, speaks_spanish)` add them after the stored text at send time, all fixed wording; `fee_free` is the caller's `catalog::api::JobType::fee_free` (FEE-045's `fee_free_job_types`) and `sent_to` the provider-accepted count T147's card-notice sender passes; `CardParts` is unchanged. Language is no input to matching (`CardJob` and `CardBusiness` carry none), so no business can filter or skip jobs by language; the E2E half of TD-CARD-03 and TD-TXT-22's counts stay with their tasks. Reason: CARD-012, CARD-019, FEE-045, D-188, D-403, D-491, D-493. Source: `docs/spec/job-cards.md:16`, `docs/spec/job-cards.md:23`, `docs/spec/fees.md:49`.
- **D-1034** Question (T185 review): the change runs past the task's 300-line budget (about 400 changed lines across the four owned files and the shared docs, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, after the review fixes). Choice: kept as one change. The card-lines test file alone is about 250 lines, because TD-CARD-02 needs a planted phrase per category with its log check, every list entry, the no-listed-phrase texts, a property test and the review's domain and hyphen cases; TD-CARD-03 and TD-CARD-07 add their own. The review fixes also put the contact cut before the restricted removal (D-1031) and move the log test from a scoped subscriber (`with_default`) to one process-wide subscriber whose writer keeps lines only on the listening test thread, since in a full-crate run the scoped subscriber raced other test threads registering the same log callsite and missed the first event. Reason: as D-1021 and D-1026, a budget overrun is logged rather than cutting a requirement's checks; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`.
- **D-1037** Question (T156): how does the question set run one question at a time, and how are two conflicting lines read? Choice: `intake::api::BankRun` (pure) asks the set in its order, applies each `ask_if`, asks only `emergency` questions on an emergency job and only after the cards (`starts_now`), ends every bank list with "Not sure" ("No sé"), counts every prompt (the smell question and the one AI follow-up included) toward 8, and stores option numbers, "Not sure" or the code `text` (free words never stored here). With AI off the template is asked word for word and the keyword rule is: exactly one option of two or more words appears as whole words in her request ("Swamp cooler pads are dry" answers "Swamp cooler"; one-word options such as "Yes" never skip). With AI on no keyword skip runs; the AI reading names its question ID and skips only at or above `BankSettings::skip_threshold`, `None` until AI-027's run, so nothing is skipped (D-492). A rewording and the follow-up go through `ai::api::accept_question` (the pure AI-019 check; no AI call is made here, so D-1030 (B) stays open); `askhava-intake` now depends on `askhava-ai`, which `kit/layers.json` already allows. Conflict 1: INT-039 says "Not sure" on every question and also gives the smell question's exact text with three options (TD-INT-18); the exact text wins for the smell list and "not sure" is still accepted as a reply. Conflict 2: INT-039 and TD-INT-18 say the smell question follows "any numbered smell answer in any set", while TD-INT-24 says a boat "Fuel smell" answer sends nothing extra; read together, it follows a smell answer that does not name its kind (`asks_smell_kind`: "smell" first or after "or", "a", "strange", "odd", "weird"), and a set that already holds the smell list (hvac `smell_kind`) asks it through its own `ask_if`. Reason: the decide-and-log rule (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:539`); both tests then hold. Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:43`; `docs/test-design.md:273`; `docs/test-design.md:276`; `docs/test-design.md:279`; D-492; D-1030.
- **D-1038** Question (T156): what are INT-040's confidence levels before a real model exists? Choice: the keyword reading scores 1.0 when one trade and exactly one job type of it are named, 0.5 for one trade with none or several, 0.0 for several trades (`keyword_scored`); the high-confidence setting defaults to `HIGH_CONFIDENCE` 0.8 and is passed in by the caller (no `ASKHAVA_*` key yet: nothing reads it until the conversation wiring, D-999, adds one). `decide` goes on only when the keyword reading and, with AI on, the AI reading agree on trade and job type at or above it; otherwise it returns the INT-013 question built by `matching::second_opinion`, and with no trade from either it returns `NoTrade` for the INT-016 path. Reason: the keyword rules are certain only when they name one job type; the AI's confidence comes from its reading (AI-022). Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:44`; D-395; D-999.
- **D-1039** Question (T156): what does the golden run measure, when does it run, and what about `test_set.csv`? Choice: `intake::api::run_golden` routes every `docs/catalog/intake_golden.yaml` row on the AI-off path (the build has no real model) and counts it right when `decide` goes on with no question at the row's trade and job type and the trade's set opens with the row's question; it stores total and right in `intake.golden_result` once per `catalog_version` (16 hex of a SHA256 over the compiled-in `categories.yaml`, `question_bank.yaml` and `intake_golden.yaml`), and the worker runs it at start-up, so a build with a changed catalog runs once. `test_set.csv` is not run yet: its trade and job-type codes are the knowledge base's own (`fridge`, `range_oven`) and map to no catalog job type; the mapping is a plan gap for the runner. Measured on this branch: 21 of 370 rows (5%), far under the 90% target, because the keyword rules cover few trades and little Spanish; the report (T210) shows the number as it is. Source: `docs/spec/ops-recovery.md:44`; D-493.
- **D-1040** Question (T156): who writes the "Job type not certain" mark and the INT-040 homeowner text? Choice: `after_fit` sets `Outgoing::not_certain` when "Not sure" or a second unusable reply keeps more than one candidate; `quotes::api::rules::match_job` with every candidate already reaches only a business covering all of them, so never one covering part of the job or outside the trade; `unsure_reach` returns `NoneCovers` when it reaches nobody. `quotes::api::CardParts` has no marker line and the homeowner's "We couldn't tell which kind of <trade> job this is" text has no template; this task owns neither quotes nor customer copy, so both are a plan gap for the runner (the card-line owner and the copy owner), and the OPS-041 email is T215's. Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:44`; `docs/spec/job-cards.md:11`; D-493.
- **D-1041** Question (T156): the prompt's size budget is at most 7 files and 450 changed lines (`kit/prompts/T156.md:50`), and the change touches about 19 files and about 1,460 lines; is it split, and what else does the change rest on? Choice: it stays one change. The 7 owned files carry the rules and their tests; the rest are what those files cannot work without: the crate's `lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the two `.sqlx/` query files the golden run needs for the offline build, the worker's start-up call (`app/server/src/bin/worker.rs`, `app/server/Cargo.toml`), the `tests/mod.rs` line and the `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` entries (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:489`). About half the lines are tests (`app/intake/src/tests/question_bank.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/routing_confidence.rs`); splitting the question set from routing confidence would leave `decide` without the set it opens (D-1039's "right" needs both) and a crate with a half-built `api`. The budget is the plan's estimate, not a rule a task breaks to keep; the overrun is reported for the runner. Golden run at start-up: `run_golden` is called before the worker loop (`app/server/src/bin/worker.rs:40`) and its error is returned, so a failed run (database down, a migration missing, a catalog that does not load) stops the worker on purpose: a worker that cannot read its own catalog must not route jobs; a low share never fails it (D-1039: the number is reported as it is). `askhava-ai` dependency: `askhava-intake` now depends on `askhava-ai` (`app/intake/Cargo.toml:10`) for the pure `ai::api::accept_question` check only, which `kit/layers.json` allows (intake is layer 7, ai lower); no AI call is made, so INT-021's wiring stays open, but the dependency D-1030 (B) said was missing now exists, so (B) is partly crossed and the task that wires the AI call into intake no longer adds it. Smell follow-up: `BankRun::after` sets the smell question due only when `smell_kind` is not already answered, so two smell answers in one set ask it once (`td_int_18_smell_question_is_asked_once`). Reason: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:485` (small PRs) weighed against a change that works and is tested as a whole; the decide-and-log rule (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:539`). Source: `kit/prompts/T156.md:50`; `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs:40`; `app/intake/Cargo.toml:10`; `kit/layers.json`; D-1030; D-1037; D-1039.
- **D-1064** Question (harness, October 31, 2026; found at 19:44Z when PR #196's `Checks` job went red on a head whose `docs/decisions.md` was 1,005,469 bytes while main's was 998,763; numbered under D-1036's interim rule above the next claim blocks (counter 1042, T046 claiming D-1048 to D-1052, a further claim D-1053 to D-1057, D-1058 open in #196, so the claim after it takes D-1059 to D-1063) because the live `--reserve-decision` of D-1058 is not merged yet): what happens when `docs/decisions.md` passes the PII scanner's 1,000,000-byte text limit, which main reaches at its next task merge? Options: (A) raise `MAX_BYTES` (`scripts/pii_scan.py:37`); (B) put `docs/decisions.md` on `SKIP_ALLOWED`; (C) split the decisions file. Decision: (A) `MAX_BYTES = 4_000_000`. The scanner skips a text file over the limit and, under D-485, a skipped file that is not allow-listed fails the run, so without this change the first task merge after 19:45Z would have turned `Ci` red on main and every open PR. (B) would stop scanning the one file every worker appends to, which D-485 exists to prevent; (C) changes every script that reads the file and the append-at-end rule (D-1029) for no gain. The file grows about 1.5 KB per task, so it ends the build near 1.3 MB; 4 MB leaves room for the whole build and its audits while a 4 MB read is still well under a second. The two size tests in `tests/test_pii_scan.py` (`:94`, `:188`) read the constant, so they stay as they are. Change: `scripts/pii_scan.py:37`, `kit/plan.lock` rewritten, plus the routine prompt re-measure (D-1036: context lines in `kit/prompts/T*.md` and `context_pct` in `kit/tasks.json`) because the decisions file grew.
- **D-1058** Question (harness, October 31, 2026; two rule changes Casey approved today, "All approved"): (A) how does a change made outside the runner get a decision number that no claim can also take, and (B) should a worker lose an attempt when the plan, not the worker, left out a file it had to change? Finding (A): `docs/governance.md:64` (section 3.6, from D-530) had such a change take "the next number above both main's highest entry and `next_decision`" and bump nothing, so it was a guess the counter never saw: today D-1030 was picked by two builders, a D-1031 would have collided with T185's block 1031 to 1035, and D-1036 had to guess past that block (D-1029 handled only the order of the entries, not their numbers). Finding (B): a worker that touches a file its `owns` did not list fails `runner/verify.py:43` ("not owned by T###") and loses one of `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` (`runner/cycle.py:16`); four tasks paid for plan errors that way (D-840, D-886, D-932, D-1023; D-1030 recorded the pattern). Choice (A): a new overseer command `python3 -m runner --reserve-decision --reason TEXT` (`runner/__main__.py:28`, `runner/__main__.py:105`, `reserve_decision` at `runner/__main__.py:291`, dispatched at `runner/__main__.py:383`; same `--session` and `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` as `--requeue`) reads main's docs/decisions.md fresh (`GitHubEnv.decision_numbers`), refuses an empty reason or an unreadable file, and through `update_state` (fetch, write, retry from a fresh read after a rejected push) calls `state.reserve_plan_number` (`runner/state.py:287`): the number is the first at or above `next_decision`, above main's highest entry and above every reserved number; it is appended to the new top-level `plan_reservations` list ({number, at, reason, session}), `next_decision` moves past it, and the command prints `reserved D-####`. `_reserved` (`runner/state.py:264`) now includes plan reservations, so `reserve_decisions` (`runner/state.py:271`, block size `DECISION_BLOCK = 5` at `runner/state.py:52`) never hands out a block over one even if the counter is lost; `scripts/check_state.py:123` counts them as reserved (no number in two places, all below `next_decision`) and `kit/state_schema.json:121` describes the list. CI acceptance is not added: `scripts/check_pr_change.py` runs in Governance from main's checkout against the head (`.github/workflows/governance.yml:49`) and in Ci with only main fetched, and neither reads `claude/kit-state`, so it cannot tell a reserved number below `next_decision` from a guessed one; the rule is the overseer's to follow, stated in `docs/governance.md:64` (amended in place, same line count) and step 4 of the plan-change routine (`docs/ai-operating-manual.md:86`), and the two hints of `scripts/check_pr_change.py:115` and `:129` now name the command. This supersedes D-530's sentence "A change made outside the runner takes the next number above both main's highest entry and `next_decision` and bumps nothing"; D-530 is not edited (the log is append-only). Choice (B): `cycle.plan_gap_failure` (`runner/cycle.py:264`, called at `runner/cycle.py:310` before `record_failure`) treats a submitted attempt whose every problem ends with ": not owned by <its own task id>" (`NOT_OWNED`, `runner/cycle.py:261`; an ending match, so a file name containing the phrase is never mistaken for one), with no model, review, protected-path or empty-hand-in problem beside it, as a plan gap: on the task's first one it goes back to QUEUED with `attempts` unchanged, `last_failure` naming the paths and saying the attempt was free, and one entry in the task's new `plan_gap_strikes` ({at, paths, attempt}, `kit/state_schema.json:386`); its history entry is marked `plan_gap` (`runner/cycle.py:1252`), so the repeated attempt number explains itself. A second path-only failure, a path failure beside any other problem, an outcome other than `submitted` (a failed test run never reaches the path check), and a task already at `MAX_ATTEMPTS` (its one plan-fix attempt, D-677, stays exactly one) count as before, so a worker that insists on scope creep still runs out. `--requeue` and `--plan-fix` are unchanged: they read `attempts`, which a plan gap leaves as it was. `docs/architecture.md:292` describes both; that paragraph is read by most prompts, so `scripts/gen_prompts.py` re-rendered the 30 whose measured share moved by a point (only their `context_pct` and the prompt's size-budget line change; no template or pasted text changed, and T185's running prompt is not among them), and `--check --strict` reports 0 problems. Tests: `tests/test_runner_decisions.py:112` (the right number, recorded, counter advanced, a second call takes the next), `:123` (above main's highest and a stale counter), `:128` (`_reserved` includes them and a claim with a lost counter skips them), `:136` (`check_state` counts them); `tests/test_runner_live.py:1275` (the command against a real git origin: refusals, two sessions get D-107 and D-108); `tests/test_failure_drills.py:354` (first path-only failure: attempts unchanged, strike recorded), `:365` (second one increments), `:376` (path plus wrong model, path plus protected path, path on a failed test run: each increments, no strike), `:389` (the rule, including the capped plan-fix case, a resync cleared and a protected-path problem whose file name contains ": not owned by T1"); no existing test changed. `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. Number: chosen by the interim rule of D-1036's entry, with headroom above the next two claim blocks, because the live `--reserve-decision` could not be run from the build session (its write to `claude/kit-state` was refused there); this is the last number chosen that way, and from the next plan change on the command decides. At the final re-check live `next_decision` was 1042 and main's highest entry D-1047, so the next claim takes D-1048 to D-1052 and a second claim (two lanes can both free before this merges) D-1053 to D-1057; this entry takes D-1058. Reason: a number the counter does not know about is a collision waiting for the next claim, and an attempt lost to a file the plan forgot charges the worker for the planner's mistake while the cap still stops a worker that ignores its scope. Source: `docs/governance.md:64`; `runner/state.py:52`; `runner/state.py:264`; `runner/state.py:271`; `runner/state.py:287`; `runner/__main__.py:291`; `runner/cycle.py:16`; `runner/cycle.py:264`; `runner/cycle.py:310`; `runner/verify.py:43`; `scripts/check_state.py:123`; `scripts/check_pr_change.py:115`; `.github/workflows/governance.yml:49`; `docs/ai-operating-manual.md:86`; D-530; D-677; D-840; D-886; D-932; D-1023; D-1029; D-1030; D-1036; Casey's approval in chat, October 31, 2026.
- **D-1075** Question (harness, October 31, 2026; Casey's standing approval for harness fixes through the normal gate; numbered under D-1036's interim rule because `--reserve-decision` (D-1058, #196) was not on `main` when this was written and, once it was, the build session's write to `claude/kit-state` was refused by its permission layer (not routed around; `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` step 4 now names this fallback and it stays as the standing fallback, replacing D-1058's "last number chosen that way", since a refused write must not stall a fix): live `kit/state.json` on `claude/kit-state` has `next_decision` 1058 and held blocks T156 D-1037 to D-1041, T046 D-1048 to D-1052 and FIX-MAIN D-1053 to D-1057; `main`'s highest is D-1047; D-1058 is open in #196 and D-1064 in #198; the highest of all of those is 1064, the next two claim blocks above it are D-1065 to D-1069 and D-1070 to D-1074 (`DECISION_BLOCK` 5, `runner/state.py:49`), so this is D-1075): why does every plan change re-render about 90 prompts and `kit/tasks.json` (PR #198 touched 94 files for a one-constant fix), and what keeps `docs/decisions.md` from passing the PII scanner's limit unnoticed again? Finding: the decisions log is not the cause. `context_bytes` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:439`) leaves every read under `PASTED_READS` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:73`), which includes `docs/decisions.md`, out of the count (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:449`); the log reaches a prompt only through the cited entries `paste_decisions` excerpts (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:157`), and no prompt task owns or reads the file. Appending 200,000 bytes to it on `main` at 7336f99 left `--check --strict` at the same 90 problems. The cause is `docs/architecture.md`: 207 of the 221 prompt tasks read it, it is counted whole (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:451`), it is the largest single term (146,350 bytes, about 18% of the window; D-1036 found the same) and every task appends its "What T### built" paragraph (about 1.7 KB), so every 8 KB of growth moves every reader's ceil-rounded percent by one, and `budget_problem` failed on any difference. Putting back `main`'s `docs/architecture.md` of f08ef01c cut the 90 problems to 6 (tasks whose own owned files had since appeared, T156 38 to 45 the largest). D-1064's "because the decisions file grew" named the wrong file. Options: (A) count only cited decision entries: already so, changes nothing; (B) store a coarser grain (nearest 5): re-renders every prompt once now, prints a number up to 4 points off on purpose, and still churns every reader at once when the architecture crosses a grain line; (C) a tolerance band in strict mode only: strict passes, but a full `gen_prompts.py` run (step 3 of the plan-change routine) would still rewrite every drifted prompt, so the churn stays; (D) the band in both: generation keeps a stored value that is within the band and the limit, strict fails a stored value outside it and, separately, any measurement over the task's limit; (E) stop counting `docs/architecture.md`: the worker does read it, so the measure would no longer be what a worker loads. Decision: (D), with `CONTEXT_DRIFT_POINTS = 3` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:69`). `settled_pct` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:470`) keeps the stored value while it and the measurement are both within `validate_tasks.context_limit` (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:379`, imported, not copied) and at most 3 points apart, else stores the measurement; `derive_context` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:479`) and the drift note (`estimate_line`, `scripts/gen_prompts.py:507`) use it; `budget_problem` (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:514`) fails a measurement over the limit first (the limit's purpose, D-1036: no worker starts on reading over 45, 50, 65 or 75), then a stored value outside the band. 3 points is 24,000 bytes, about 14 task merges of architecture growth, so most plan changes re-render only the prompts they change, and a worker's printed "N% of the context window" is never more than 3 points from the truth. The size of the window and the measurement itself are unchanged. Guard: `pii_scan.size_warnings` (`scripts/pii_scan.py:279`) names each file in `GROWING_FILES` (`scripts/pii_scan.py:275`, `docs/decisions.md`) over 75% of `MAX_BYTES` (`scripts/pii_scan.py:39`, read from the module, never copied); `pii_scan.py` prints it on every run (`scripts/pii_scan.py:307`), which `Ci` runs directly (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:76`; no workflow edit), and `gen_prompts.py --check --strict` prints it too (`scripts/gen_prompts.py:541`), because `scripts/smoke.sh:68` discards `pii_scan.py`'s output and a plan-change session reads the strict output. It warns and does not fail: a fail at 75% would turn `Ci` red by surprise the same way D-1064 avoided. On this branch (`MAX_BYTES` still 1,000,000 until #198 merges) it warns now, at 998,763 bytes; with #198's 4,000,000 it is quiet until 3,000,000. This entry itself takes the file past 1,000,000 bytes, so `pii_scan.py` fails on this branch until #198 merges; this branch lands after #198, with `main` merged in. Change: `scripts/gen_prompts.py` (docstring, `:56` to `:58` imports, `:69`, `:470`, `:479`, `:507`, `:514`, `:541`), `scripts/pii_scan.py` (`:275`, `:279`, `:307`; the constants sit away from `MAX_BYTES` so #198's one-line change merges cleanly), `docs/ai-operating-manual.md:87` (the routine's step 5 now states the band, the limit and the warning), `docs/architecture.md:476` (section 12), `docs/for-casey-review.md`, and `kit/plan.lock` rewritten. Reason: a check that churns 94 files for a one-line fix hides the real change from its reviewer, and the number a worker reads only needs to be close; the limit is what must hold, and it now binds the measurement directly. - **D-1088** Question (harness, October 31, 2026; found at 20:02Z when FIX-MAIN attempt 1 (PR #199, reverting T156's merge 26b176e) failed `Checks` and `Governance` with "docs/decisions.md is append-only; entry 760 was changed, moved or removed: D-1037 …"; numbered under the interim rule (D-1036, D-1064, D-1075; the live `--reserve-decision` is refused by this session's permission layer and was not routed around): counter 1058, held blocks D-1048 to D-1057, main's highest D-1075 (#201), so the next two claims take D-1076 to D-1085; the four changes in flight take D-1086 (flaky adapters test), D-1087 (one CI run per head), D-1088 (this) and D-1089 (capped FIX-MAIN recovery)): how can FIX-MAIN ever revert a task merge, when every task merge appends decision entries and `git revert` of the squash removes them, which `scripts/check_pr_change.py` (`decisions_append_only`) forbids? Options: (A) the FIX-MAIN goal tells the worker to restore `docs/decisions.md` from `main` after the revert, so the reverted task's entries stand as history and FIX-MAIN appends its own; (B) exempt the FIX-MAIN branch from the append-only rule; (C) have the runner build the revert commit itself. Decision: (A). The log is a history and the reverted entries record decisions that were made, so removing them was never right; (B) would let the one branch that touches every file of a merge rewrite history; (C) is more runner code for a case the worker can do in two commands. Change: `runner/cycle.py` `_fix_main_fields` goal text (revert, then `git checkout origin/main -- docs/decisions.md`, then append an entry); `tests/test_failure_drills.py` `test_drill_red_main_reverts_clears_and_continues` asserts the restore step; the goal also tells the worker to add a `Plan-Change` trailer when the revert touches a protected or locked path (`scripts/check_pr_change.py:51` treats `claude/task/FIX-MAIN-revert` as a plan-change branch); the goal also tells the worker to add a `Plan-Change` trailer when the revert touches a protected or locked path (`scripts/check_pr_change.py:51` treats `claude/task/FIX-MAIN-revert` as a plan-change branch); `docs/governance.md` section 5 point 2 and `docs/architecture.md` section 7 say so. `main` had never been red before today, so this path had never run for real; the drill fakes the git side. - **D-1087** Question (harness, October 31, 2026; numbered by the interim rule of D-1036 as D-1064 applied it, because the live `--reserve-decision` counter write of D-1058 was refused by this session's permission layer and D-1075 keeps that rule as the standing fallback: counter `next_decision` 1058, blocks held D-1048 to D-1057 (T046, FIX-MAIN), main's highest entry D-1075 (#201), so the next two claims take D-1076 to D-1085; the four changes in flight take D-1086 (the flaky-test fix), D-1087 (this), D-1088 (FIX-MAIN keeps docs/decisions.md, #202) and D-1089 (capped FIX-MAIN recovery)): why does every task head get two full sets of `Ci`/`Checks`/`Coverage`/`Twin`/`Ally` runs, and how is it made one? Finding: `ci.yml`, `twin.yml` and `a11y.yml` started on both `push` to `claude/**` and `pull_request`, so each head ran twice. Evidence: T156's head 7274a85 had push run 41234354024 (green) and pull_request run 41234358862, whose `Coverage` failed on a flaky test; auto-merge merged on the green set, then `runner/verify.py:85` to `runner/verify.py:90` (`check_done`: every run of `Ci`, `Twin`, `Ally` on the head must be success) found "Ci: not green on head", set main red and FIX-MAIN reverted a good merge. T185's head d4ccf3b: push `ci` finished 19:27:21Z, the squash merge 19:27:47Z, the pull_request `ci` 19:33:17Z, and `governance.yml` (`workflow_run` on `ci`) then ran `check_pr_change.py` against a main that already held the branch's entries and posted a false `Governance` failure at 19:33:34Z (7274a85 got the same, "D-1037 is new on this branch but main already has a D-1037 entry"); each head also started `backup-runner.yml` twice, one start cancelled. Options: (i) drop `pull_request`, keep `push`; (ii) keep both with a `concurrency` group on the head SHA; (iii) keep both with a job `if` that skips pull_request runs of `claude/**` heads. Decision: (i). (ii) cancels one run, which leaves a `cancelled` check run named `Ci` on the head: `check_done` fails it and `checks_state` (`runner/verify.py:104`) calls it failed. (iii) leaves a `skipped` check run named `Ci`/`Twin`/`Ally` on the head (GitHub reports a job skipped by `if` as a check run with conclusion skipped, which branch protection accepts but `check_done` does not, and `checks_state` keeps pending forever); a workflow has no workflow-level `if`, and `pull_request` branch filters match the base branch, not the head. (i) is safe for merging: a check run belongs to its commit, and the `protect-main` ruleset requires `Ci`, `Twin`, `Ally`, `Governance` by name from the GitHub Actions app (integration 15368) on the head SHA whatever event started them, with up-to-date branches required (strict), so the push run tests exactly the tree that lands; every pull request this repository has had (197 read through REST today) came from `claude/**` (193) or `dependabot/**` (4), so `dependabot/**` joins the push filter and no pull request loses its checks. Nothing depends on the `pull_request` event: `governance.yml` reads only `workflow_run.head_sha`/`head_branch`, `auto-pr.yml` starts on push, `backup-runner.yml` uses `workflow_run.head_branch` and only `pull_request: closed`, and `runner/github_env.py:690` and `runner/github_env.py:746` read check runs by commit. A pull_request run takes its workflow file from the merge ref, so open pull requests on older branches stop getting a second run as soon as this lands. Governance guard: with one `ci` run per head, `Ci` and then `Governance` both finish before auto-merge can merge, so the late-run race is gone; the guard stays as a cheap backstop for a manual re-run after a merge and for a pull_request run already started when this lands, since `governance.yml` always runs from main. Change: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5` to `.github/workflows/ci.yml:14`, `.github/workflows/twin.yml:5` to `.github/workflows/twin.yml:14`, `.github/workflows/a11y.yml:4` to `.github/workflows/a11y.yml:13` (push to `claude/**` and `dependabot/**` only; job names unchanged); `.github/workflows/governance.yml:13` (`pull-requests: read`), `.github/workflows/governance.yml:26` to `.github/workflows/governance.yml:43` (a first step asks `commits/<head>/pulls` for a merged pull request with that head and, if one exists, the later steps at `.github/workflows/governance.yml:46`, `:55`, `:60`, `:69` and the publish step at `:76` do nothing, so no check run is posted; any non-count answer counts as not merged and the rules run as before; the skip assumes a merged head is on main, which is false only when a FIX-MAIN revert is followed by the same SHA proposed again, and a retry merges main first so it gets a new SHA); `BUILD_BRIEF.md:259` and `BUILD_BRIEF.md:593` state the new trigger (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:259` also says a pull request from a branch outside `claude/**` or `dependabot/**` gets no checks and cannot merge, so use a `claude/` prefix), the `main_checks_green` docstring at `runner/github_env.py:670` to `runner/github_env.py:671` now says pushes only, `docs/architecture.md:336` describes it, and `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten, plus the routine prompt re-measure (D-1036: `kit/prompts/T*.md` and `context_pct` in `kit/tasks.json`) because the decisions file grew. The pull request for this change shows it: its head gets one `ci`, one `twin` and one `a11y` run, all with event push.

- **D-1086** Question (fix, October 31, 2026; Casey's standing approval for harness and fix improvements through the normal gate; numbered under the interim rule of D-1036's entry as widened in D-1064 and D-1075 (`docs/ai-operating-manual.md:86`), because the live `python3 -m runner --reserve-decision` is refused by this session's permission layer and is not routed around: live `kit/state.json` has `next_decision` 1058, no `plan_reservations`, and held blocks T156 D-1037 to D-1041, T046 D-1048 to D-1052 and FIX-MAIN D-1053 to D-1057; `main`'s highest entry is D-1075, so the next two claim blocks are D-1076 to D-1080 and D-1081 to D-1085 (`DECISION_BLOCK` 5); the numbers in flight outside the runner are assigned D-1086 to D-1089 (this flaky-test fix D-1086, one CI run per head D-1087, FIX-MAIN keeps decisions D-1088 in PR #202, capped FIX-MAIN recovery D-1089), so this is D-1086): why does `tests::adapter_config::voice_client_dials_from_the_pool_over_http` fail now and then with `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: NotSent` at `app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs:309` (on the old file; the first request, `open_call`), about six smoke false reds and `main` red after T156's merge 26b176e (Coverage job 124634908164 of run 41234358862, where it failed 0.12 s after the binary started), while the same head passes when re-run? Finding: `NotSent` is `send_error`'s answer to a refused connection (`app/adapters/src/base.rs:114`), so nothing was listening on the port the test was given. The test helper `stand_in` (`app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs:226` on the old file, and an identical copy at `app/adapters/src/tests/ssrf_guard.rs:465`) looked up a free port by binding port 0 and closing it, started `python3 -m stand_ins.server --port <it>`, and called the server ready as soon as any TCP connect to that port succeeded. The other 28 tests of the same binary run in parallel and also bind port 0 (three local fake hosts in `ssrf_guard.rs`, `unreachable_vendor_is_not_sent` and the other stand-ins), so another socket can take the port between the lookup and the child's bind; the child then exits with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, the connect probe succeeds against the other test's socket, and when that socket closes the test's first request is refused. In the failing CI run the probe returned within 0.12 s, sooner than the Python server can import and bind, which only a foreign socket explains. Reproduction (local, 2 cores, Rust 1.99 from `rust-toolchain.toml`, not under llvm-cov): the single test 50 times alone and the whole lib suite 30 times one at a time, 0 failures (the race needs other sockets at the same moment); the whole lib suite in 6 parallel loops of 25 (150 runs): 2 stand-in failures, one with the child's `Errno 98` traceback followed by this test's `ConnectionRefused` on port 44507 (the CI symptom) and one `payments_client_talks_to_the_stand_in` `Decode` (the request reached a socket that was not its stand-in), about 1.3%; a forced replay with the real `stand_ins.server` (another socket holds the port for 0.6 s while the child starts): the old probe reports ready and the request is refused, every time. The parallel loops also failed `ssrf_guard::slow_redirect_chains_time_out_overall` and `redirect_off_the_allowed_hosts_is_not_followed` often (wall-clock bounds of 700 ms and 2 s with 6 suites on 2 cores); those are CPU-overload timing failures of a different kind, never seen in CI, and are not changed here. Options: (A) sleep or retry the failing request, refused (it hides the race and is a retry-until-pass); (B) have the server bind port 0 and print the port it got, which needs a change to the protected `stand_ins/server.py:349` (it prints the `--port` argument, not the bound port); (C) keep the server as it is and make readiness the child's own line, `stand-ins listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, which `stand_ins/server.py:350` prints with `flush=True` only after the `ThreadingHTTPServer` constructor has bound and is listening, and start again on a new port when the child exits without it. Decision: (C). `stand_in` (`app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs:247`) makes at most `STAND_IN_STARTS = 5` (`:231`) starts, each on a newly looked-up port, through `start_and_wait` (`:272`): it spawns the command with stdout and stderr piped, reads the first stdout line on a helper thread (which then drains stdout to the end, so the child never writes to a closed pipe) and waits for it with `recv_timeout` up to `STAND_IN_READY` (10 s, `:236`; the old connect loop allowed 5 s and the server normally prints within a fraction of a second, so the bound only stops a child that neither prints nor exits). It accepts the server only when the line names exactly the port it was given; then the child's stderr is copied to the test's own on a thread (`pass_stderr_through`, `:308`), as the inherited stderr was before. Any other outcome (a different line, an empty line because the child exited, or no line in time) kills and reaps the child and returns its stdout line and stderr; after five failed starts `stand_in` panics with all five, so an `Address already in use` traceback or an import error shows in the log. There is no sleep. Once the child has bound the port no other socket can (the server sets `SO_REUSEADDR`, not `SO_REUSEPORT`), so every request of the test reaches its own server. Two new tests drive `start_and_wait` with a plain `python3 -c` child and no server or port race: `a_silent_stand_in_start_is_killed_and_reported` (`:317`, a child that sleeps 60 s is killed after a 300 ms wait and reported as "no line within") and `a_stand_in_that_exits_early_is_reported_with_its_stderr` (`:329`, a child that exits with a fake bind failure is reported with an empty stdout line and its stderr). The copy in `ssrf_guard.rs` is removed and those three tests use the shared helper (`app/adapters/src/tests/ssrf_guard.rs:19`), so all six stand-in tests of the crate start the server the same way. No existing assertion or test name and no production line changed; no test is weakened, skipped or retried. After the fix (measured before the bounded read was added; the bounded version was re-run as listed under Checks): the single test 50 times, the whole lib suite 10 times with default threads and 10 times with `--test-threads=1`, 0 failures; the 6-by-25 parallel loops, 0 stand-in failures and no `Errno 98` (only the overload timing failures above); the forced replay starts on a second port and the request is answered. Checks on the bounded version: `cargo test -p askhava-adapters --lib` 5 times, 31 passed each time (the 29 old tests and the 2 new ones); the voice test alone 50 times, 0 failures; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. Not fixed here: `app/ai/src/tests/adapter_calls.rs:312` has the same `stand_in` copy (a different test binary whose tests need PostgreSQL; the same race exists there with fewer parallel sockets) and `unreachable_vendor_is_not_sent` (`app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs:434`) still relies on a closed port staying closed, a much narrower window; both are left for a later fix. Ownership: `app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs` is owned by T016 and `app/adapters/src/tests/ssrf_guard.rs` by T176 in `kit/tasks.json`; `app/adapters/CLAUDE.md` is a shared path; this fix touches them under the FIX-MAIN rule and the reviewer decides. Coverage: only test files and the crate `CLAUDE.md` change, and `tests/coverage_floor.json` measures `app/` with tests excluded and has no `app/adapters/` floor, so it is unaffected; `cargo llvm-cov` is not installed in the build session, so the Coverage job itself was not re-run here. `docs/architecture.md` section 7 describes the voice client, not this test helper, so it is unchanged; the crate `CLAUDE.md` names the helper and why. Change: `app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs`, `app/adapters/src/tests/ssrf_guard.rs`, `app/adapters/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Reason: the flake was a port race in the test harness, not in the voice client, and a readiness signal from the child itself removes it without touching a protected path; never weaken a test (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`). After this entry was numbered, `main`'s highest became D-1088 (#202), still below 1086's slot in the in-flight list; the number stands. Source: `app/adapters/src/base.rs:114`; `stand_ins/server.py:332`; `stand_ins/server.py:349`; `stand_ins/server.py:350`; `docs/ai-operating-manual.md:86`; D-1036; D-1058; D-1064; D-1075.
- **D-1110** Question (pacing, October 31, 2026; Casey 14:10: "We only have about 50% of our weekly AI budget left, and it resets on Thursday … if there is something that is wasting tokens that can be stopped without negatively affecting the project, we should probably do that"; numbered under the interim rule (D-1036, D-1064, D-1075; the live `--reserve-decision` is refused by this session's permission layer and not routed around): counter 1058, held blocks to D-1057, main's highest D-1099, so the next two claims take D-1100 to D-1109 and this is D-1110): what weekly budget should the pacer use, now that there is a real reading? `kit/pacing.json` called its 450M (`budget_tokens_week` 500M less 10% headroom) a placeholder, and the quota probe (`scripts/quota_probe.py`) has never reported in the runner (`state.usage.source` is "ledger" on every row), so the pacer has been measuring against a number about twice the plan. Casey's 50% reading came while the ledger stood at 102M weighted tokens in the week window that started 2026-10-29T18:38Z and resets 2026-11-05T18:38Z. Options: (A) `budget_tokens_week` 200M (the reading, rounded down: the ledger does not count the overseer sessions' own tokens, so the plan is a little further along than it shows); (B) leave 500M and let the plan cut the runner off; (C) pace evenly to Thursday. Decision: (A). The pacer's job is to stop claiming before a cut-off, because a cut-off mid-attempt wastes the whole attempt (1 to 3M weighted tokens); with (A) it claims while the next estimate fits and then waits for the reset, which Casey accepts. (C) finishes no more tasks for the same tokens and slows the chain while budget remains. The five-hour budget keeps its placeholder for want of a reading. Not changed, logged as the next step: find out why `quota_probe.py` falls back (likely the Actions session's credentials file or the endpoint shape; D-486 said to fix the probe, not `pacing.py`). What was not waste: the ~1.3M weighted tokens a task attempt costs is the worker plus the required Opus review; retries (12% of attempts so far) are the real waste and today's D-1086, D-1087 and D-1088 target their causes; a third lane spends the same tokens sooner, so it stays parked while the plan cap is the constraint. Change: `kit/pacing.json` (`budget_tokens_week`, `budget_source`, note), `kit/plan.lock` if it covers that file.

Choice: `quotes::api::window_open(sent_at, now)` is `now < sent_at + 24 hours`, absolute time every day of the week, so a card sent at 08:00 takes a quote at 07:59:59 the next day and refuses one at 08:00:00; `sent_at` is `quotes.job_card.sent_at`, and the card-notice sender that holds a card for quiet hours (T147) records the actual send there, as D-1021 left it. `submit_quote` refuses a business with no card, a closed window, or a job whose status fails the new `JobStatus::takes_quotes` (Open, No quotes yet, Quotes ready, Awaiting confirm; Confirm moves the job to Payment pending, D-043), reading the status through `jobs::api::current` in the quote's transaction; a Confirm committed between that read and the insert orders as a Confirm just after the quote, as D-1021 does for late cards. - **D-1049** Question (T046, PICK-002, PICK-051, TD-PICK-02): the shape of `quotes.quote`, when a quote counts as business-confirmed, and where the PICK-040 facts and `quotes.quote_bounce` (architecture section 3) go. Choice: `migrations/0070_quotes_quote.sql` adds one row per business per job: the format code, amount or low and high (an hourly quote's are rate times hours), tier names and prices (1 to 3), period, setup charge, hourly rate and hours, the on-site tick, notes, original wording, `ai_read`, `confirmed`, earliest visit (date and part of day), `received_at`, `edited_at`, `withdrawn_at`, and no expiry column; a second quote from the same business is an edit (`edited_at`), and one sent after the business withdrew clears `withdrawn_at` (the quote is back, re-checked like any edit, inside its window and before any pick), rather than being refused. PICK-051 allows an edit only before any pick: `submit_quote` answers `Submitted::EditClosed` to a business that already quoted once the job fails the new `JobStatus::takes_quote_edits` (Open, No quotes yet, Quotes ready) or any quote on the job carries `unavailable_at` (a failed pick, D-1051), while a first quote from another business is still taken up to Confirm (D-043). A form quote is confirmed as sent; an AI-read one (`ai_read`) is not until `confirm_quote` (T148's read-back screen, PICK-006, D-149), and an edit of one needs confirming again; `confirm_quote` reads the job status in its transaction and moves on once `takes_quotes` fails, but not at the window end, since the quote itself came in inside the window. An unconfirmed quote counts as neither quoted nor choosable when the windows end; one confirmed after that check is shown and choosable while the job still waits in Quotes ready, and the TXT-042 count already sent is not redone. `shown_quotes` returns only confirmed, unwithdrawn quotes. `QuoteForm` and `Price` have hand-written `Debug` that leaves out the notes, original wording and tier names, which may hold the contact detail PICK-007 refuses (rust brain R6). The other PICK-040 facts get their columns with the form that collects them (T148, which also adds the minutes column) and their display with T186. No bounce table is built, although architecture section 3 (a locked section) lists `quotes.quote_bounce` for `quotes`: a bounced quote holds the contact detail PICK-007 refuses, and a table holding only the bounce reason and time with no value adds nothing the form needs, so the bounce is returned to the form and not stored; the section 3 row is left for a plan change if Casey wants a value-free bounce count (noted in `docs/for-casey-review.md`). Size: the task's budget is 7 files and 400 changed lines; the owned files reach about 1,580 lines (the review fixes included), mostly tests and the doc comments `docs/code-docs.md` requires; the work was not split because the window, the stored record and the trigger share one transaction and one test file. - **D-1155** Question (harness change, November 1, 2026; numbered under the corrected interim rule: max(`next_decision` 1132, main's highest 1144 + 1, open plan PRs' highest + 1) + 10 = 1155, with D-1154 kept for the war-games plan change in preparation): why does the pacer still read its own ledger (`usage.source` "ledger"), and how does it get the plan's real figure? Finding: D-1128's probe note on the 23:54Z claim says "no token: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN unset and no credentials file": the action gets the login as its own input, and the Bash tool's subprocesses, where `python3 -m runner` and the probe run, do not receive it, so `scripts/quota_probe.py` has never had a token in the runner (D-486's rehearsal never confirmed it). Passing the secret to the probe under another variable name was refused by this session's permission layer as a security weakening, and `BUILD_BRIEF.md:62` keeps keys out of plain environment variables, so that route is not taken. The action streams `rate_limit_event` messages with the plan's own windows (`unifiedWindows.seven_day.utilization` 0.51 and `resetsAt` at 22:22Z on October 31, the number Casey reads under /usage) and writes every message to its execution file (`steps.<id>.outputs.execution_file`), which the job can read after the session ends, with no token. Choice: (1) `runner/usage_reading.py` `latest_reading` keeps the last `rate_limit_event` of an execution file (a JSON array or one message per line; `unifiedWindows` first, else a bare `rateLimitType` window; utilisation clamped to 0..1; `resetsAt` epoch seconds to ISO) as pacing's windows, and `python3 -m runner --usage-reading FILE` writes it through `update_state` as `usage.session_reading` {"at", "week", "five_hour" when reported}; a file with no event changes nothing. (2) `backup-runner.yml`: the action step gets `id: claude` and a step after it, `if: always()`, runs the command on `steps.claude.outputs.execution_file` when the file exists. (3) `scripts/pacing.py` `session_reading` returns the stored reading while it is under `SESSION_READING_HOURS` (6) old; `standing` uses it for the windows it holds after a probe reading and before the ledger, and the source string says "session_reading <at> (<windows>)". The reading arrives at the end of each session, so the next claim paces on the plan's own percentage; the spend line (D-1128) then measures against that figure, and its anchor can be moved to a plan reading once the first one lands. Tests: `tests/test_usage_reading.py` (parser over array and JSONL, bare window, clamp, record, pacing's use and staleness, the probe still winning); `tests/test_workflow_shell.py` covers the new bash step. Kind: harness. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for fixes through the normal review gate, reported afterwards; Casey asked for the plan percentage to drive pacing (October 31). Reason: D-486, D-1110, D-1128; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:62`. Source: `scripts/quota_probe.py`, `scripts/pacing.py:187`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` (the action step), the job log of run 41247709349 at 22:22Z, `kit/state.json` `pacing.last` at 23:54Z.

- **D-1178** Question (harness fix, November 1, 2026; numbered under the corrected interim rule: max(`next_decision` 1132, main's highest 1167 + 1, open plan PRs' highest + 1) + 10 = 1178, D-1154 kept for the war-games plan change): why did the runner cycle of run 41260929485 (01:24Z) write no row and no state? Finding: its start-routine smoke test (`scripts/smoke.sh` on main's head: fmt, clippy, build, sqlx check, the whole test suite, audit, deny) outran `run_command`'s 600-second subprocess timeout, and `smoke_main` (`runner/github_env.py`) let `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` escape, so the cycle died with a traceback, no `runner_log` row and no pacing decision; the job's later steps still ran (the usage reading was recorded). The smoke has been slow for two reasons the reviewer separated: `smoke_main` runs the script in a detached worktree under a temporary directory and nothing set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, so every smoke compiled the workspace from cold into that directory and the job's cached `target` (4.3 GB restored each run) served it nothing but the registry; and the Rust build cache (D-514) is keyed by `rust-toolchain.toml` and `Cargo.lock` alone while `actions/cache` never updates an existing key, so the saved `target` is a snapshot from the last dependency change and the workers' builds grow from it until the next lock change. Choice: (0) `run_command` gives the smoke CARGO_TARGET_DIR = `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target` (an explicit value kept), so it builds on the job's cached target (`_smoke_env`). (1) `backup-runner.yml`'s cache key ends in `${{ github.sha }}`, with restore keys by lock hash then by OS, so every run that may save (a dispatch or scheduled run; a pull-request run's token cannot) leaves a fresh snapshot and the next restores the newest; the repository's 10 GB cache evicts the oldest. (2) `SMOKE_TIMEOUT` 540 seconds for `bash scripts/smoke.sh` in `run_command` (under the session's 600-second Bash call, so the runner answers before the call is killed and the session does not start a second smoke), and `smoke_main` turns `TimeoutExpired` into a smoke result of exit 124 ("smoke timed out after N seconds") flagged `smoke_timed_out`; the cycle records the run with `timed_out`, claims nothing, never counts it as a D-498 strike (three such strikes would have turned `main` red and queued FIX-MAIN against an innocent merge) and never sets `main` red for it; after `SMOKE_TIMEOUTS_BEFORE_NOTE` (3) timeouts on one head it writes one `info` outbox item, since a smoke that never finishes starves the build; a later red result on the head is judged as before, and a timeout in the verify smoke after FIX-MAIN merged leaves `main` red without raising `revert_landed_red` (the reviewer's point). Tests: `tests/test_runner_live.py` `test_a_smoke_test_that_outruns_its_budget_is_a_red_smoke_not_a_crash` and `test_run_command_gives_the_smoke_its_own_timeout` (incl. CARGO_TARGET_DIR); `tests/test_failure_drills.py` `test_drill_a_smoke_timeout_is_noted_never_a_strike_and_never_red`. Left open (reviewer): `subprocess.run`'s timeout kills only `bash`, so cargo may run on as an orphan while the worktree is removed — a process group for the smoke is a follow-up; 540 s leaves about a minute for the cycle's other work inside the session's 600-second call, measured in later runner_log rows. Kind: harness fix. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for fixes through the normal review gate, reported in the hourly update. Reason: D-514, D-498, D-486 (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:240`, the smoke at the start routine). Source: job log of run 41260929485 (the traceback at 01:36:42Z and the cache lines), `runner/github_env.py:106`, `runner/github_env.py:672`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` (the cache step), `kit/runner_log.jsonl` rows at 01:01:52Z and 01:56:58Z.
- **D-1154** Question (plan change, November 1, 2026; Casey's instruction in chat at 16:45 Phoenix on October 31, and his addition at 17:11; number reserved for this change by the coordinator under the interim rule of `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` section 7 step 4 and kept free on `main` by D-1155, D-1156, D-1167 and D-1178, which say so): after the build is done and before anything goes live or Twilio is hooked up for real, how does Ask Hava run "war games" (every kind of customer and business, people pranking it or trying to burn AI credits, completed jobs with simulated money visible in the owner portal, an extended period of running the business as chaotically as possible to break it and find loose ends), and where does the live AI key's billing come from? Choice: six stage-6 tasks between the restore drill (T139) and the fresh Opus audit (T140), which now depends on the last of them so the audit sees every fix: **T234** (harness) builds `wargames/` (Python, standard library; a new top-level folder, added to `docs/architecture.md` section 2; not protected, but every task touching it is a harness task with an Opus reviewer): a persona library for both sides, a scenario runner over the test site's real entry points with a local lane on the stand-ins for faults sandboxes cannot make, chaos injectors and anomaly checks that log request, job and message IDs; **T235** (harness) runs jobs to completion through Stripe test mode and reconciles the ledger, Stripe test mode, the owner portal's money view and every statement CSV to the cent (FEE-021 to FEE-030, FEE-051, BIZ-015), with `docs/phase2/money-war-game.md`; **T236** (build, `ai`) adds the credit-drain defense the spec lacked; **T237**, **T238**, **T239** (harness, each owning `wargames/`, `app/`, `migrations/` and the Rust test folders so fixes land with their regression tests in the round that finds them, like the cleanup tasks) run the campaign in three rounds of at least 5 simulated business days and 100 completed jobs each (40 paid; 15 days and 300 jobs over the campaign), every finding a WG-### row in `docs/phase2/war-games.md` with its IDs and the requirement it breaks; T239 is the clean run and writes the report (cast, runs, findings, fixes, money, credit-drain proof, final run). Findings are fixed through the normal task gate inside the round's task (Opus worker, Opus review, `Ci`, `Twin`, `Ally`); a finding whose fix would change a requirement, a test-design entry or a locked file is not fixed by the round but goes to the top of `docs/for-casey-review.md` as a plan-change item, because a task cannot change the plan (`docs/governance.md` section 1); a final round that still finds something says so and a further round needs a plan change, since the runner cannot add tasks itself. **New requirement AI-028** (`docs/spec/ai.md`) and **TD-AI-18**: the spec had per-phone request limits (SEC-014, SEC-015), the global daily AI-call cap (AI-021) and no AI call for an unverified web chat (AI-021), but nothing stopped one phone from burning the day's whole AI cap inside its 5 requests an hour, so AI-028 adds per-step budgets sized to the spec's own AI-on flow, which needs about 12 calls before the card (2 readings per message under AI-011, 1 reword per bank question up to 8 under INT-039, 1 follow-up, card and project file 1 each plus 1 per EDIT up to 3 under INT-041, 4 concept prompts under INT-046, 2 screening calls a photo for up to 3 photos under AI-016), with backstops of 40 calls per conversation per Arizona day and 60 per job; the card call is always reserved, so no budget lands on it and no EDIT is left half done; no AI call before the consent text and the area check; a verified web-chat session shares the budget of the phone it verified with and an unverified one makes none (as AI-021 already says); quote reads (PICK-006) have their own 3 per business per job and never count toward the job's budget, so a prank homeowner cannot stop honest businesses' quotes being read; only the first 1,600 characters of a scrubbed message go to the AI, a trade-off that can leave a late fact out of an AI-written card, so the AI-off card and the stored request keep her full scrubbed words; past a budget the step runs on the AI-off path silently (INT-021), and `budget` rows never count toward the AI-021 daily cap (T236 changes `calls_today` to exclude them). An independent review of the first draft (one flat cap of 12 calls a conversation and 30 a job, which the AI-on flow itself would have hit) found it blocking; this is the redesign; it is a new rule on WHAT in a locked file, sourced to Casey's instruction, and **the reviewer is asked to confirm that adding it is in scope** (the changes file does not speak to AI cost; BUILD_BRIEF.md:331 asks for rate limits per phone). Threat model row D12 added. **Credit (Casey, 17:11):** his Claude subscription includes $200 a month of API credit, so the live product's Claude API key is to be created under that subscription's Anthropic account and production AI usage draws on the credit: the account-checkpoint gate (T127) gains one `steps` line in its message (gate mechanics unchanged; `runner/github_env.py` `gate_body` already prints `steps`), `docs/PREBUILD.md`'s accounts row says so, and T141's goal adds the Gate C checklist item (`docs/account-checklist.md` Part 2, owned by T122 and updated by T141) with a check on the Console's billing page. Also: `BUILD_BRIEF.md` Phase 2 step 7 names the war games (edited in place, line count kept); `docs/build-readiness.md` section 3's stage-6 row now counts 24 tasks and names the campaign's exit; T142's deps add T234 to T239. War-games tests run offline in `Ci`; `wargames/runs/` is git-ignored; on the test site the AI-008 switch is on during the rounds, real Claude calls on fake data, with the campaign's AI spend capped at $40 (a test-project AI-021 cap of 600 calls a day and the Console spend limit, the lower) and texts on Twilio test credentials and magic numbers only; round tasks never change an existing test except through a logged spec change (BUILD_BRIEF.md:69). Validator: the round tasks are harness type because they own directories (only cleanup and harness may) and run past MAX_FILES; T236 holds 7 owned files at budget 7; `migrations/0197_ai_call_budget.sql` follows 0196 in serial order; money and security review areas give every new task an Opus reviewer. Kind: plan change (new tasks, a new requirement, owner instruction). Owner approval: Casey, October 31 (war games, 16:45; the API credit, 17:11). - **D-1190** Question (T047, TXT-017, D-012, TD-TXT-06): the 3-hour gap is "measured from the delivery time of the previous update", but the first-quote text is not an update, delivery times live in `messaging` (below `quotes`), and T047 owns no migration. Reason: fewer texts is the safe side of TXT-017 and quiet hours; no new storage. Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:21`.
